name: Pinoin 0.025% Cream 20gm
description: Introduction About PINOIN 0.025% CREAM PINOIN 0.025% CREAM contains Tretinoin, which belongs to the group of medicines called Retinoids. It is used to manage acne. It can also be used to manage wrinkles, skin spots and rough skin. Acne is defined as a skin disease involving inflammation of the sebaceous follicles of the face and upper body, characterized by lesions on the face, back, upper chest and shoulders. Before using PINOIN 0.025% CREAM, inform your doctor if you have any sunburn, sun sensitivity or any other skin problems. PINOIN 0.025% CREAM should be used in pregnancy only if specifically directed by your doctor. PINOIN 0.025% CREAM should be used with caution in breastfeeding women. The safety and effectiveness of PINOIN 0.025% CREAM in children (aged less than 12 years) have not been established, so consult your doctor before using it. The most common side effect of using PINOIN 0.025% CREAM is skin irritation like redness, burning, stinging, dryness and peeling. Contact your doctor if any of the side effects worsen. Uses Of PINOIN 0.025% CREAM It is used to manage acne, wrinkles, skin spots and rough skin. How PINOIN 0.025% CREAM Works PINOIN 0.025% CREAM works by modifying the abnormal cavity formation that comes from the excessive conversion of cytoplasm to keratin (a strong protein that is the main substance that forms hair, skin, etc.) of epithelial cells, promoting detachment of tough cells and enhancing shedding. How to use PINOIN 0.025% CREAM Apply PINOIN 0.025% CREAM as advised by your physician. It is for external use only. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration for you depending on your age, body weight and disease condition. Side Effects Of PINOIN 0.025% CREAM Common Skin irritation like redness, burning, stinging, dryness and peeling Rare Stop using PINOIN 0.025% CREAM and contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following side effects: Excessive redness, swelling, blistering or crusting Allergic reaction (rash, hives or peeling skin with or without fever, wheezing, chest or throat tightness, trouble breathing, swallowing or talking, abnormal hoarseness, swelling of the mouth, face, lips, tongue or throat) Warning & Precautions Pregnancy PINOIN 0.025% CREAM should be used in pregnant women only if specifically directed by your doctor. Consult your doctor before using it. Breastfeeding PINOIN 0.025% CREAM should be used with caution in breastfeeding women. Consult your doctor before using it. Allergy Do not use PINOIN 0.025% CREAM if you are allergic to Tretinoin or any of the other ingredients of this medicine. Others PINOIN 0.025% CREAM is not recommended for use if you: Are sunburned Have eczema or other skin conditions Before applying PINOIN 0.025% CREAM, inform your doctor if you: Have sun-sensitive skin Use in pediatrics: The safety and effectiveness of PINOIN 0.025% CREAM in children (aged less than 12 years) have not been established. Consult your doctor before using it. Use in geriatrics: The safety and effectiveness of PINOIN 0.025% CREAM in elderly patients (65 years and older) have not been established. Consult your doctor before using it. Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Before using PINOIN 0.025% CREAM, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines: Other medicines used to manage acne (Ex. benzoyl peroxide, resorcinol, salicylic acid) Medicated or abrasive soaps and cleansers Medicines containing high concentrations of alcohol, astringents or spices B. Drug-Food interactions: Avoid contact of the skin with the lime peel during management with PINOIN 0.025% CREAM. Overdosage: If you or anyone else accidentally applied too much of PINOIN 0.025% CREAM, contact your doctor immediately. Symptoms of overdose include irritation or increased irritation of your skin. Synopsis Drug : Tretinoin Pharmacological Category : Retinoids Therapeutic Indication : Acne Dosage Forms : Capsule, Cream, Gel, Gel (Topical) More Information Keep PINOIN 0.025% CREAM out of reach of children Store below 25°C FAQs About PINOIN 0.025% CREAM Q: Can the use of PINOIN 0.025% CREAM manage wrinkles? A: PINOIN 0.025% CREAM contains tretinoin, which is a derivative of vitamin A and is commonly used for various skin conditions, including acne and photoaging (skin aging caused by sun exposure). Tretinoin is known for its ability to stimulate collagen production and promote skin cell turnover, which can lead to improvements in skin texture and appearance. For wrinkles, tretinoin can be effective in reducing fine lines and improving skin elasticity. It works by increasing cell turnover and promoting the production of collagen, which can help to smooth out wrinkles over time. However, it does not completely manage wrinkles. Q: How long does it take for PINOIN 0.025% CREAM to show results? A: Results from PINOIN 0.025% CREAM, containing tretinoin, vary among individuals. Generally, noticeable improvements in skin texture and wrinkle reduction may take several weeks to months. In the initial 2-4 weeks, users may experience skin adjustment, potentially including redness or flakiness. Over the first 2-3 months, fine lines may begin to diminish as collagen production increases. Long-term and consistent use (3-6 months and beyond) is often necessary for the most significant improvements. Following dermatologist instructions and using sunscreen is crucial due to increased skin sensitivity. Individual responses differ, so patience is essential, and any concerns should be addressed with a dermatologist. Q: Can PINOIN 0.025% CREAM remove dark spots? A: PINOIN 0.025% CREAM containing tretinoin, can help reduce the appearance of dark spots by promoting skin cell turnover and inhibiting melanin production. While it may not completely manage dark spots, consistent and long-term use, along with sun protection, can lead to noticeable improvements. For a comprehensive approach, consulting with a dermatologist is recommended. Q: Can I use PINOIN 0.025% CREAM daily? A: PINOIN 0.025% CREAM should be used under careful medical supervision. Your doctor might recommend you to consistently use this medicine for a longer period of time to achieve best results. Following dermatologist instructions and using sunscreen is crucial due to increased skin sensitivity. It is important to stay with patience to notice results and if any concerns arise, kindly consult your doctor. Q: Does retinol brighten your skin? Yes, retinol is a vitamin A derivative with powerful antioxidant properties. It can contribute to skin brightening by promoting cell turnover and reducing hyperpigmentation, resulting in a more even complexion. Q: What is acne? Acne is a common skin condition characterized by the presence of pimples, blackheads, whiteheads, and inflammation, often caused by clogged hair follicles and the overproduction of oil. It is primarily caused by a combination of factors, including excess oil production, clogged hair follicles, bacteria (Propionibacterium acnes), and inflammation. Hormonal changes, genetics, certain medications, and lifestyle factors can also contribute to the development of acne. Q: What precautions should I take while using PINOIN 0.025% CREAM? A: Do not use PINOIN 0.025% CREAM on sunburned skin, cuts, scrapes, eczema or damaged skin. Practice good skin care and avoid exposure to sunlight as you may get sunburned more easily. Use sunscreen and wear clothing and eyewear to protect your skin from the sun. Some weather conditions may irritate your skin. Talk with your doctor in such a case. Q: Can I use makeup during management with PINOIN 0.025% CREAM? A: While using PINOIN 0.025% CREAM, it is advisable to be cautious with makeup application, especially during the initial stages of management as the tretinoin present in the medicine can make your skin more sensitive and prone to irritation. Q: Can I use other skin preparations with PINOIN 0.025% CREAM? A: Do not use any other skin preparations with PINOIN 0.025% CREAM without asking your doctor. Avoid preparations that may dry or irritate your skin, like those containing astringents, alcohol, spices or lime or certain medicated soaps, shampoos, etc. Do not allow anyone else to use this medication. Do not use other medicines containing retinoids which are not recommended by your doctor, as it might cause unnecessary redness or peeling. Q: Can the use of PINOIN 0.025% CREAM make your skin dry? A: Dry skin especially on your nose and lips is a prevalent side effect of using PINOIN 0.025% CREAM. It happens because the tretinoin present in the medicine reduces sebum secretion on your skin. To combat this, keep yourself hydrated by drinking plenty of water and fluids, Apply a moisturizer and lip balm that suits your skin as advised by your physician. Q. Is PINOIN 0.025% CREAM safe? A: The safety of using PINOIN 0.025% CREAM depends on individual factors and skin sensitivity. Consultation with a dermatologist is recommended to determine its suitability for your specific skin type and concerns. The most common side effect of using PINOIN 0.025% CREAM is skin irritation like redness, burning, stinging, dryness and peeling. Contact your doctor if any of the side effects worsen. Q. Can PINOIN 0.025% CREAM be used in pregnant women? A: PINOIN 0.025% CREAM is not recommended for use in pregnant women as it may harm the growing baby. Therefore, it is important to consult your doctor before using PINOIN 0.025% CREAM if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. References 1. Barbara G. Wells, Joseph T. DiPiro, Terry L. name: Ezanic 20% Cream 15gm
description: Introduction About EZANIC 20% CREAM EZANIC 20% CREAM contains Azelaic acid which belongs to the group of medicines called Dicarboxylic acids. It is used to manage common acne (acne vulgaris). It is also used for the management of mild to moderate papulopustular rosacea. Acne is a skin condition that occurs when the hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells. It causes whiteheads, blackheads or pimples. Rosacea is a skin condition that causes blushing or redness, pus-filled bumps and small visible blood vessels in the face. EZANIC 20% CREAM should be applied with caution in patients with lung problems such as asthma. Consult your doctor before applying it. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before applying this medicine. Your doctor will decide whether you can use this medicine. EZANIC 20% CREAM is generally not recommended for use in children under 12 years of age for the management of acne and also not recommended for use in children under 18 years of age for the management of rosacea. Consult your doctor before applying it. The most common side effects of applying EZANIC 20% CREAM are burning, itching or redness of the skin (erythema) at the application site, scaling, pain, dryness, skin discolouration or irritation at the application site. Contact your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen. Uses Of EZANIC 20% CREAM Common acne (acne vulgaris) Mild to moderate papulopustular rosacea How EZANIC 20% CREAM Works EZANIC 20% CREAM attacks the bacteria called propionibacterium acnes, which plays an essential part in causing acne. It also reduces growth of the harder outermost skin cells (keratin surface cells) that block the pores of the skin to cause blackheads and whiteheads. How to use EZANIC 20% CREAM Apply EZANIC 20% CREAM as directed by your physician. It is for external use only. Wash your hands with soap and water before and after using EZANIC 20% CREAM. Apply a thin layer of this medicine on the affected area and rub it gently into the skin. Avoid applying this medicine around your eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes or open wounds. If it does, wash the eyes, mouth or other mucous membranes immediately with large amounts of cool water. name: BENZONIX XL GEL Wash 100g
description: Introduction About BENZONIX XL GEL WASH BENZONIX GEL Wash is used in the management of acne. It is used on the face, chest, or back where the skin has a lot of blackheads, spots, and pimples. It contains Benzoyl peroxide, which belongs to the group of medicines called Anti-bacterial and Anti-inflammatory agents that attack the bacteria known as Propionibacterium acnes, one of the main causes of acne. BENZONIX GEL Wash is not recommended for severe acne and/or on the skin with deeper pits and dents, broken and/or damaged skin, or for people who are allergic to benzoyl peroxide and/or any other ingredient found in BENZONIX GEL Wash. It is not recommended for use by pregnant and breastfeeding women unless necessary. Consult your doctor before using BENZONIX GEL Wash. It is recommended to use only those products that are labelled as non-comedogenic to prevent clogging of pores. Avoid applying BENZONIX GEL Wash around your eyes, including eyelids and other mucous membranes. Also, care must be taken not to apply BENZONIX GEL Wash to broken or damaged skin or to skin with dents or scars. The most common side effects of using BENZONIX GEL Wash are skin tension, burning, stinging, itching, peeling, and reddening of the skin. Consult your doctor if any of the above reactions bother you. Uses Of BENZONIX XL GEL WASH To manage acne How BENZONIX XL GEL WASH Works BENZONIX GEL Wash works against acne-causing bacteria. This medicine, after being applied to the affected skin, gets absorbed and is converted to benzoic acid. This benzoic acid gets metabolized by skin proteins and releases active free-radical oxygen species that result in the alteration of bacterial proteins. This helps to manage acne or pimples. BENZONIX GEL Wash also acts as a keratolytic agent, which promotes peeling of the skin and absorbs excess oil from the skin, further preventing acne formation and skin irritation. How to use BENZONIX XL GEL WASH Always use BENZONIX GEL Wash as directed by your physician. It is for external use only. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration for you, depending on your disease condition. Wet the area to be managed. Wash hands before use and place a small amount of BENZONIX GEL Wash your hands to wash the affected area. Wash and rinse thoroughly with water after application. Apply calamine lotion to help reduce itching and inflammation. Applying cool compresses and wearing loose, breathable clothing can also provide relief. If the rash persists, consult your doctor. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy CONTRAINDICATED BENZONIX XL GEL Wash is not recommended for use by pregnant women unless necessary. Consult your doctor before using it. Breastfeeding CONTRAINDICATED BENZONIX XL GEL Wash is generally not recommended to be used in nursing women. Consult your doctor before using this medicine. Allergy CONTRAINDICATED Do not use BENZONIX XL GEL Wash if you are allergic to benzyl peroxide or to any other ingredients in this medicine. Use In Pediatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR Your doctor will decide the right dose depending on your child’s age, body weight, and disease condition. Consult your doctor before using BENZONIX XL GEL Wash. Overdosage: If you or anyone else accidentally uses too much of BENZONIX XL GEL Wash or accidentally ingests it, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. It is best taken with food, preferably at the same time each day, to reduce the chances of missing a dose. It may take a few weeks before you notice an improvement in your symptoms but continue taking the medication as directed to achieve optimal results. If your condition does not improve after several weeks, consult your doctor for further advice. This medication can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, so limit sun exposure and use sunscreen when outdoors. It may also make your skin more fragile, so avoid waxing or laser treatments during therapy. Dryness of the lips, mouth, and eyes is another potential side effect—stay hydrated and use moisturizers or lubricating eye drops as needed Common side effects include dry skin, rashes, and elevated liver enzymes. While these are generally mild and tend to subside as your body adjusts to the medication, inform your doctor if they persist or cause discomfort. ACNETOIN I 10 SOFTGEL CAPSULE is known to cause birth defects, so it should not be used during pregnancy or if you are planning to conceive. Always discuss your treatment plan with your doctor to ensure safety and effectiveness. It works by reducing the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, unclogging pores, and decreasing inflammation, which helps to clear up existing acne and prevent new breakouts. This leads to smoother, healthier skin and reduces the risk of long-term scarring. Always consult your doctor to ensure it is suitable for your condition. How ACNETOIN I 10 SOFTGEL CAPSULE Works ACNETOIN I 10 SOFTGEL CAPSULE work by targeting the root causes of severe acne. They reduce the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, which helps prevent pores from becoming clogged. This, in turn, reduces the growth of acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Together, these actions help clear up existing acne and reduce the chances of scarring, making it an effective treatment for stubborn or severe acne conditions. Follow the prescribed dosage and duration carefully. Do not stop the medication abruptly without consulting your doctor, even if your symptoms improve. Regular follow-ups and blood tests may be required to monitor your progress and ensure safe usage. Avoid alcohol, excessive sun exposure, and waxing or laser treatments during the treatment period. Use sunscreen and moisturizers as recommended by your doctor. What if I Forget to take ACNETOIN I 10 SOFTGEL CAPSULE: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. description: Introduction About AZIDERM 15% GEL AZIDERM 15% GEL contains Azelaic acid which belongs to the group of medicines called Dicarboxylic acids. It is used to manage common acne (acne vulgaris). It is also used for the management of mild to moderate papulopustular rosacea. Acne is a skin condition that occurs when the hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells. It causes whiteheads, blackheads or pimples. Rosacea is a skin condition that causes blushing or redness, pus-filled bumps and small visible blood vessels in the face. AZIDERM 15% GEL should be applied with caution in patients with lung problems such as asthma. Consult your doctor before applying it. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before applying this medicine. Your doctor will decide whether you can use this medicine. AZIDERM 15% GEL is generally not recommended for use in children under 12 years of age for the management of acne and also not recommended for use in children under 18 years of age for the management of rosacea. Consult your doctor before applying it. The most common side effects of applying AZIDERM 15% GEL are burning, itching or redness of the skin (erythema) at the application site, scaling, pain, dryness, skin discolouration or irritation at the application site. Contact your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen. Uses Of AZIDERM 15% GEL Common acne (acne vulgaris) Mild to moderate papulopustular rosacea How AZIDERM 15% GEL Works AZIDERM 15% GEL attacks the bacteria called propionibacterium acnes, which plays an essential part in causing acne. It also reduces growth of the harder outermost skin cells (keratin surface cells) that block the pores of the skin to cause blackheads and whiteheads. How to use AZIDERM 15% GEL Apply AZIDERM 15% GEL as directed by your physician. It is for external use only. Wash your hands with soap and water before and after using AZIDERM 15% GEL. Apply a thin layer of this medicine on the affected area and rub it gently into the skin. Avoid applying this medicine around your eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes or open wounds. If it does, wash the eyes, mouth or other mucous membranes immediately with large amounts of cool water. Side Effects Of AZIDERM 15% GEL Common Burning, itching or redness of the skin (erythema) at the application site Scaling, pain, dryness, skin discolouration or irritation at the application site Uncommon Greasy skin Acne or loss of skin colour Tingling Dermatitis Discomfort or swelling at the application site Rare Cracking of the lips, small blisters Eczema, ulceration Warmth at the site of application Allergic reaction such as urticaria or hives, rash at the site of application Worsening of asthma Stop applying AZIDERM 15% GEL and contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following side effects: Allergic reaction such as rash, angioedema (swelling under the skin), swelling of face, eyes and dyspnoea (shortness of breath) How To Manage Side Effects Skin rash: Avoid hot bath because hot water can irritate your skin further. Do not scratch the affected area. Use sunscreen and wear protective clothing while going outside. Use unscented moisturizers to soothe and hydrate the affected area. Contact your doctor if the rashes worsen. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or are planning to have a baby before applying this medicine. Your doctor will decide whether you can use AZIDERM 15% GEL. Breastfeeding AZIDERM 15% GEL should be used with caution in breastfeeding women. Consult your doctor before applying it. Infants must not come into contact with managed skin or breasts. Driving and Using Machines AZIDERM 15% GEL has no influence on the ability to drive and use machines. Allergy Do not apply AZIDERM 15% GEL if you are allergic to Azelaic acid or any of the other ingredients of this medicine. Lungs AZIDERM 15% GEL should be applied with caution in patients with lung problems such as asthma. Consult your doctor before applying it. Others Use in pediatrics: AZIDERM 15% GEL is generally not recommended for use in children under 12 years of age for the management of acne. It is also not recommended for use in children under 18 years of age for the management of rosacea due to a lack of data on safety and efficacy. Consult your doctor before applying it. Use in geriatrics: There is limited information available on the use of AZIDERM 15% GEL in elderly patients. Consult your doctor before applying it. Interactions A. Drug - Drug interactions: Tell your doctor if you are taking or have recently taken any other medicines, including medicines obtained without a prescription, vitamin supplement or herbal products. Overdosage: If you or anyone else accidentally used too much of AZIDERM 15% GEL or if you or a child accidentally swallow the medicine, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Synopsis Drug : Azelaic acid Pharmacological Category : Dicarboxylic acids Therapeutic Indication : Common acne, Papulopustular rosacea Dosage Forms : Cream, Gel, Gel (Topical) More Information Keep AZIDERM 15% GEL out of the sight and reach of children Store AZIDERM 15% GEL below 30°C FAQs About AZIDERM 15% GEL How long can I use AZIDERM 15% GEL? How long AZIDERM 15% GEL has to be used varies from person to person. It depends upon how bad your acne is when you start management. In general, you may notice a distinct improvement after 4 weeks. In case of no improvement after 1 month or if the acne or rosacea becomes worse, you should discontinue AZIDERM 15% GEL and consult your doctor. How long does it take AZIDERM 15% GEL to lighten skin? AZIDERM 15% GEL when applied twice daily for several (up to 8 months), skin lightening starts after 1 to 2 months of using it. Contact your doctor before applying it. Does AZIDERM 15% GEL cause redness of skin? Yes. AZIDERM 15% GEL may cause burning, itching or redness of the skin (erythema) at the application site. Contact your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen. Is AZIDERM 15% GEL safe in pregnancy? Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or are planning to have a baby before applying this medicine. Your doctor will decide whether you can use AZIDERM 15% GEL. Can I apply face creams while using AZIDERM 15% GEL? Yes, you may apply cosmetics after the AZIDERM 15% GEL has dried. name: Sotret 20mg Capsule 10'S
description: Introduction About SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE contains Isotretinoin, a retinoid medication specifically designed to manage severe acne in adults and children over 12 years of age. It is particularly effective for nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring when other anti-acne treatments have failed. Acne is a skin condition characterized by inflammatory spots, oily skin, and painful nodular lesions that commonly affect the face, chest, and back. Take SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE exactly as prescribed by your doctor, following the recommended dose and duration. It is best taken with food, preferably at the same time each day, to reduce the chances of missing a dose. It may take a few weeks before you notice an improvement in your symptoms but continue taking the medication as directed to achieve optimal results. If your condition does not improve after several weeks, consult your doctor for further advice. This medication can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, so limit sun exposure and use sunscreen when outdoors. It may also make your skin more fragile, so avoid waxing or laser treatments during therapy. Dryness of the lips, mouth, and eyes is another potential side effect—stay hydrated and use moisturizers or lubricating eye drops as needed Common side effects include dry skin, rashes, and elevated liver enzymes. While these are generally mild and tend to subside as your body adjusts to the medication, inform your doctor if they persist or cause discomfort. SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE is known to cause birth defects, so it should not be used during pregnancy or if you are planning to conceive. Always discuss your treatment plan with your doctor to ensure safety and effectiveness. Uses Of SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE Severe acne in adults and children (older than 12 years of age) Benefits of SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE for Acne: SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE is highly effective in managing severe acne conditions such as nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring. It works by reducing the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, unclogging pores, and decreasing inflammation, which helps to clear up existing acne and prevent new breakouts. This leads to smoother, healthier skin and reduces the risk of long-term scarring. Additionally, it targets the underlying causes of severe acne, making it a reliable choice for those who have not responded to other treatments. Always consult your doctor to ensure it is suitable for your condition. How SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE Works SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE work by targeting the root causes of severe acne. They reduce the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, which helps prevent pores from becoming clogged. This, in turn, reduces the growth of acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Isotretinoin also promotes the turnover of skin cells, preventing the formation of new acne lesions. Together, these actions help clear up existing acne and reduce the chances of scarring, making it an effective treatment for stubborn or severe acne conditions. How to use SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE Take SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the capsule whole with a glass of water; do not crush or chew it. It is recommended to take the capsule with food to improve absorption and reduce stomach discomfort. Take it at the same time each day to maintain consistent levels of the medication in your body. Follow the prescribed dosage and duration carefully. Do not stop the medication abruptly without consulting your doctor, even if your symptoms improve. Regular follow-ups and blood tests may be required to monitor your progress and ensure safe usage. Avoid alcohol, excessive sun exposure, and waxing or laser treatments during the treatment period. Use sunscreen and moisturizers as recommended by your doctor. What if I Forget to take SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose—do not double the dose to make up for it. Overdosage of SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE – In case you or anybody else accidently take too much of SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Symptoms of SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE overdose are severe headache, abdominal pain, nausea, dizziness, redness of face, vomiting, somnolence, irritability, and itching. Side Effects Of SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE Like all medicines SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE may cause certain side effects, although not everyone gets them Common Side Effects of SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE: Dry skin More fragile and red skin than usual, especially of the face Back, muscle or joint pain (particularly in children and teenagers) Raised liver enzymes Changed blood fat and cholesterol levels Easy bruising, bleeding or clotting Headache Protein or blood in the urine Becoming more prone to get infections Sore or inflamed throat and nose Stop taking SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE and consult your doctor immediately in case you experience any of the following: Persistent pain in your lower back or buttocks (signs of sacroiliitis) Severe skin reactions (Ex. erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis) (blistering and peeling of skin, severe rashes, fever, multiple lesions especially in mouth, nose, eyes and genitals, conjunctivitis, flu-like symptoms) Feeling depressed with suicidal thoughts Serious reactions (trouble breathing or swallowing due to sudden swelling of the throat, face, lips and mouth, sudden swelling of the hands, feet and ankles, hives, bruises, eczema, bruising, red patches on hands and legs) Rhabdomyolysis (muscle weakness along with trouble moving arms or legs, painful, swollen, bruised areas of the body, dark urine, reduced or no urination, confusion or dehydration) Hepatitis (yellow skin or eyes, tiredness) Kidney inflammation (difficulty urinating, swollen and puffy eyelids, excessive tiredness) How To Manage Side Effects Dry Skin Hydrate Regularly: Drink plenty of water throughout the day to keep your skin hydrated from within. Aim for at least 8–10 glasses daily. Use a Gentle Cleanser: Opt for a mild, fragrance-free cleanser to avoid further irritation. Avoid harsh soaps or scrubs that can strip the skin of natural oils. Moisturize Frequently: Apply a rich, non-comedogenic moisturizer to your face and body at least twice a day, especially after washing. Look for products with hydrating ingredients like hyaluronic acid or ceramides. Protect Your Lips: Use a moisturizing lip balm, preferably one with SPF, to prevent and treat cracked lips caused by dryness. Reapply as needed throughout the day. Avoid Long, Hot Showers: Hot water can strip your skin of its natural moisture. Take shorter showers with lukewarm water to minimize dryness. Humidify Your Environment: Use a humidifier in your home to add moisture to the air, especially during winter or in dry climates. Apply Sunscreen: Use a broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher daily to protect your sensitive skin from sun damage and prevent further dryness. Limit Exfoliation: Avoid physical or chemical exfoliants, as isotretinoin makes your skin more delicate and prone to irritation. Choose Gentle Fabrics: Wear soft, breathable fabrics like cotton to reduce friction and irritation on your dry skin. Seek Medical Advice: If dryness becomes severe or persistent despite home remedies, consult your doctor for additional treatment options or product recommendations. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy CONTRAINDICATED Human and animal studies have shown that isotretinoin is teratogenic in nature. Birth defects such as abnormalities of the face, eyes, ears, skull, central nervous system, cardiovascular system, and thymus and parathyroid glands or IQ less than score of 85 have been reported in female patients who were pregnant or became pregnant while on therapy with isotretinoin. Therefore, SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE is considered unsafe for use during pregnancy. Women of childbearing potential must use a reliable contraceptive method to avoid becoming pregnant. If you accidentally became pregnant while taking this medicine, stop taking it and consult your gynaecologist for further evaluation. It is also not recommended for you to get pregnant for one month after stopping isotretinoin tablets because some medicine may still be left in your body. Consult your doctor before taking it. Breastfeeding CONTRAINDICATED It is not known whether this medicine is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects, nursing mothers should not receive SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE Driving and Using Machines USE WITH CAUTION Do not drive or operate machinery if you experience dizziness, drowsiness or decreased night vision after taking SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE. Alcohol CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR Avoid consuming alcohol while taking SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE as it may increase side effects. Inform your doctor if you have an habit of chronic alcoholism. Kidney USE WITH CAUTION SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE should be used with caution in patients with kidney problems. Consult your doctor before taking it. Liver CONTRAINDICATED SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients with liver disease. Consult your doctor before taking it. Allergy CONTRAINDICATED Do not take SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE if you are allergic to Isotretinoin, soya, peanuts or any of the other ingredients of this medicine. Lungs USE WITH CAUTION SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE should be used with caution in patients having asthma. Consult your doctor before taking it. Use In Pediatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR The use of isotretinoin tablets in pediatric patients less than 12 years of age has not been studied. The use of isotretinoin for severe recalcitrant nodular acne in adolescents ages 12 to 17 years under careful medical supervision. Extreme caution should be taken if the child is suffering from metabolic or structural bone disease. Use In Geriatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR There is no proper information about the use of SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE in elderly patients. Consult your doctor before taking it. Others SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use if you have: High blood fat levels High levels of Vitamin A Before taking SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE inform your doctor if you: Have or had mental illness or family history of mental illness such as depression, mood disorders, psychosis, aggressive behaviour, or hurting or killing self Have diabetes Are fructose intolerant Are overweight Safety Advice Always take isotretinoin with a meal to improve its absorption. Drink plenty of water to prevent dryness in your mouth and throat. Isotretinoin is related to vitamin A, so extra supplementation can cause toxicity. Avoid Excessive Sun Exposure: Wear sunscreen and protective clothing as isotretinoin can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Moisturize Regularly: Use lip balms and non-comedogenic moisturizers to manage dryness of lips and skin. Use Effective Birth Control: Isotretinoin can cause severe birth defects. Therefore, women must use reliable contraception as isotretinoin can cause severe birth defects. Do Not Donate Blood: Avoid donating blood while on isotretinoin and for at least a month after stopping it, as it can harm pregnant recipients. Follow Regular Check-Ups: Attend scheduled visits with your doctor for blood tests and monitoring. Avoid Waxing or Laser Treatments: Your skin is fragile during treatment and prone to scarring. Alcohol can increase the risk of liver problems, so limit or avoid it. Notify your doctor about severe dryness, mood changes, or unusual symptoms. Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Before taking SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines: Vitamin A supplements Medicines used to manage bacterial infections (Ex. minocycline, doxycycline) Phenytoin (used to manage fits) Medicines used to manage various inflammatory conditions (Ex. betamethasone, prednisolone, dexamethasone) Medicines used to manage pregnancy (Ex. Norethindrone, ethinyl Oestradiol) St. John’s wort (herbal medicine used to manage mental disorders) Other medicines used to manage acne like keratolytic or exfoliative agents (Ex. salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide) Synopsis Drug : Isotretinoin Pharmacological Category : Retinoids Therapeutic Indication : Severe acne Dosage Forms : Tablet, Soft gel Capsule, Capsule More Information Relevant Health Articles – Hormonal Acne: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment Anti-Acne Food: Eat Healthy To Heal Acne -Infographic FAQs About SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE Q: What is SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE used for? A: SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE is used to manage severe acne (nodular or cystic acne) that does not respond to other treatments like antibiotics. It works by reducing oil production in the skin and preventing clogged pores. Q: How should I take SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE? A: Take SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE as prescribed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily with food. Swallow the capsule whole with water, and avoid breaking or crushing it. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully for the best results. Q: What are the common side effects of SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE? A: Common side effects include dry skin, chapped lips, dry eyes, nosebleeds, and mild stomach discomfort. If you experience severe reactions like mood changes, persistent headaches, or vision problems, consult your doctor immediately. Q: Can SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE be taken during pregnancy? A: No, SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE should not be taken during pregnancy as it can cause severe birth defects. Women of childbearing age must use effective contraception during and at least one month after treatment. Q: Is SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE safe for long-term use? A: Isotretinoin is not usually prescribed for long-term use due to its potential side effects. Treatment duration is typically limited to 16–20 weeks. Always follow your doctor’s advice regarding treatment duration. Q: Can I use cosmetics while on SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE? A: Yes, you can use non-comedogenic and fragrance-free cosmetics. Avoid abrasive cleansers, harsh exfoliants, or acne products containing benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid, as these may irritate your skin. Q: Does SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE cause hair loss? A: Temporary hair thinning or hair loss can occur in some individuals during treatment. This side effect typically resolves after completing the course. If hair loss persists, consult your doctor. Q: Can I drink alcohol while taking SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE? A: It is advised to avoid alcohol while taking SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE, as it can increase the risk of liver damage and worsen side effects like dizziness or drowsiness. Q: How long does it take for SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE to work? A: You may start noticing improvements within 4–8 weeks, but the full effects are usually seen after completing the treatment course. Be patient and continue using the medicine as prescribed. Q: What precautions should I take while using SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE? A: Avoid excessive sun exposure and use sunscreen. Do not donate blood during and for one month after treatment. Inform your doctor about any other medications or supplements you are taking. Use a reliable birth control to avoid becoming pregnant while taking SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE. Do not undergo cosmetic procedures such as skin waxing, dermabrasion, laser, or artificial UV light detanning while taking SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE without consulting your doctor. Q: Can SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE be used by men? A: Yes, SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE is safe for men to use for severe acne. However, male patients planning to father a child need not take special precautions, as isotretinoin does not affect sperm. Can SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE cause irregular periods? According to some studies, menstrual irregularity was observed during management follow-ups. Consult your doctor if you experience irregularity in your periods during management with SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE. Is SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE safe to take in pregnancy? No. SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use in pregnant women and women planning a pregnancy. Inform your doctor if you become pregnant during management with SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE. It is not recommended to get pregnant for one month after stopping SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE management because some medicine may still be left in your body. Consult your doctor before taking it. Contraception must be used for a month before taking SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE, during management and for a month afterwards. Discuss with your doctor regarding suitable contraceptive methods. Can I play sports during SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE management? Cut down on extreme exercise and physical activity as SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE can cause muscle and joint pain especially in children and teenagers taking up vigorous physical activity. Consult your doctor if you can play sports during this management. Can I go out in the sun during SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE management? Sensitivity to light may increase during management with SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE so, avoid going too much into the sun and don’t use a sun-lamp or sun-bed. Before you go out in the sun, wear sunglasses and use sunscreen with a high protection factor (SPF 15 or higher). Can undergo cosmetic procedures while taking SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE? No. Do not undergo cosmetic procedures such as skin waxing, dermabrasion, laser, or artificial UV light detanning while taking SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE or at least for 6 months after stopping it as they could cause scarring, skin irritation, or changes in your skin colour. Consult your doctor before undergoing any cosmetic procedure while taking SOTRET 20MG CAPSULE. References 1. KD Tripathi. Drugs Acting on Skin and Mucous Membranes. name: Perobar 2.5% Bar 75gm
description: Introduction About PEROBAR 2.5% BAR Perobar Soap is a cleansing soap used to manage acne. It is also used to soothe, cleanse, or nourish the skin. It contains Benzoyl Peroxide as active ingredient that kills the infection causing bacteria, removes dirt, excess oil and unclog pores. Benzoyl Peroxide gets converted into benzoic acid which releases active free-radical oxygen. These free radicals interfere with important bacterial function and survival, hence killing them. It also increases the turnover rate of skin cells which helps in managing acne. Use Perobar Soap as advised by your physician. It is for external use only. Wet the skin and apply it on the affected areas. Work up a good lather with it and leave for few minutes, then rinse with water and pat dry the application area. Use it 2-3 times daily. Do not exceed the daily recommended dosages. Consult your doctor if you experience any allergic reactions while using it. Key Composition Benzoyl peroxide Therapeutic Uses Of PEROBAR 2.5% BAR Manages acne Soothes, cleanses, and nourishes the skin Side Effects Of PEROBAR 2.5% BAR Perobar Soap may cause local dryness, irritation, eczema (skin inflammation), redness, skin peeling, and itching. Consult your doctor if you notice any such side effects while using this soap. Safety Advice Always use it as advised by your doctor It is for external use only Use it 2-3 times daily or as advised by your doctor Wet the skin and apply it on the affected areas Work up a good lather with it and leave for few minutes Rinse with water and pat dry the application area Do not use this medicine beyond the daily recommended dose Do not use Perobar Soap if you are allergic to any of its ingredient It should be used with caution in pregnant and breast-feeding women. Consult with your doctor before using It is not recommended for use in children below 12 years of age. Ask for the advice of your child’s doctor priorly Inform your doctor about all the medicines you use, including prescription, over-the-counter medications and vitamin D/calcium supplements More Information Keep Perobar Soap out of sight and reach in children Store at room temperature between 15-30°C FAQs About PEROBAR 2.5% BAR Q. What is Perobar Soap used for? A. Perobar Soap is a cleansing soap used to manage acne. It is also used to soothe, cleanse, or nourish the skin. It contains Benzoyl Peroxide as active ingredient that kills the infection causing bacteria, removes dirt, excess oil and unclog pores. Q. What are the side effects of Perobar Soap? A. Perobar Soap may cause local dryness, irritation, eczema (skin inflammation), redness, skin peeling, and itching. Consult your doctor if any of the condition worsens. Q. What precautions do I need to follow while using Perobar Soap? A. While you are using Perobar Soap, avoid unnecessary exposure to sun. You should always use sunscreens while using this product. Avoid its contact with hair and clothes as it may cause bleaching. Q. How long should I use Perobar Soap? A. Perobar Soap should be used for as long as it is recommended by your doctor. It might start showing up results by third week and reach its maximum efficiency in eight to twelve weeks. Do not use it for a prolonged period rather than as recommended by your doctor. Q. With regular use, it might also make your skin appear brighter and nourished. name: GLOCIN Gel 30gm
description: Introduction About GLOCIN GEL GLOCIN GEL is a combination of Clindamycin and Nicotinamide which belongs to a group of medicines called Lincomycin antibiotics and Vitamin B3 complex, respectively. GLOCIN GEL is used to manage mild to moderate acne which is a skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells which may occur due to variety of causes such as genetics, fluctuating hormone levels, stress, high humidity or using oily or greasy personal care products which may affect people of all ages. It is characterized by symptoms such as open or closed plugged pores, small red & tender bumps, pimples, large, solid or painful lumps under the skin and painful & pus-filled lumps under the skin. Before using GLOCIN GEL inform your doctor if you have liver, kidney, lung or heart diseases. Avoid applying GLOCIN GEL to a cut, scrapped, sunburnt or eczema affected skin. GLOCIN GEL should be used with caution in pregnant and in breastfeeding women. GLOCIN GEL is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (below 12 years). Consult your doctor before applying. The most common side effects of using GLOCIN GEL are skin inflammation, contact dermatitis (red, itchy rash), inflammation of hair follicles, itchy skin, dry skin and peeling of skin. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsen. Uses Of GLOCIN GEL Manage mild to moderate acne How GLOCIN GEL Works GLOCIN GEL helps to manage acne, where Clindamycin reduces free fatty acid concentrations on the skin and suppresses the growth of Propionibacterium acnes (Corynebacterium acnes), a bacteria found in sebaceous glands and follicles and Nicotinamide exerts anti-inflammatory effect in acne and interrupts sebum production. How to use GLOCIN GEL Apply GLOCIN GEL as advised by your physician. It is for external use only. Before applying the medicine normally wash and dry the affected area and apply a thin layer of this medicine on the affected area. Managed areas on the face need not be covered with a plaster or bandage. Do not apply this medicine beyond the recommended duration. Avoid applying GLOCIN GEL around your eyes, including eyelids. Rinse it off with water if you accidentally get it in these areas. Side Effects Of GLOCIN GEL Common Contact dermatitis (red, itchy rash) Inflammation of hair follicles Itchy skin Dry skin Peeling of skin How To Manage Side Effects Skin rash/Itchy skin: Avoid hot bath because hot water can irritate your skin further. Do not scratch the affected area. Use protective clothing when going outdoors. Regularly moisturize your skin and apply calamine lotion as a coolant. Discuss with your doctor if the symptom worsens. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy GLOCIN GEL should be used with caution in pregnant women. Consult your doctor before applying. description: Introduction About SALID 12 OINTMENT SALID 12 OINTMENT contains Salicylic acid which belongs to the group of medicines called Keratolytic agents. SALID 12 OINTMENT is used manage skin conditions such as psoriasis, dry, scaly skin conditions and acne. It is also used to manage dandruff, corn and calluses (thickened layers of skin) in affected individuals. SALID 12 OINTMENT is not recommended for use in patients allergic to Salicylic acid. It is also not recommended for use in patients with active inflammation/dermatitis, infection (at the application site), acute viral infection, skin malignancy, and/or tanned skin. Before applying SALID 12 OINTMENT, inform your doctor if you are scheduled for surgery, and/or suffering from any kidney problems. SALID 12 OINTMENT is generally not recommended for use in pregnant women. If you are a breastfeeding women, consult your doctor before using the medicine. Avoid applying the medicine on skin areas which might come in direct contact with infant’s skin. SALID 12 OINTMENT should be used with caution in children and adolescents (aged 1-15 years). It is also advised to be used with caution in elderly patients (aged above 65 years). Consult your doctor before applying the medicine. The most common side effects of applying SALID 12 OINTMENT are erythema (skin redness) or skin dryness. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsens. description: Introduction About REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL contains Tretinoin, which belongs to the group of medicines called Retinoids. It is used to manage acne. It can also be used to manage wrinkles, skin spots and rough skin. Acne is defined as a skin disease involving inflammation of the sebaceous follicles of the face and upper body, characterized by lesions on the face, back, upper chest and shoulders. Before using REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL, inform your doctor if you have any sunburn, sun sensitivity or any other skin problems. REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL should be used in pregnancy only if specifically directed by your doctor. REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL should be used with caution in breastfeeding women. The safety and effectiveness of REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL in children (aged less than 12 years) have not been established, so consult your doctor before using it. The most common side effect of using REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL is skin irritation like redness, burning, stinging, dryness and peeling. Contact your doctor if any of the side effects worsen. Uses Of REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL It is used to manage acne, wrinkles, skin spots and rough skin. How REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL Works REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL works by modifying the abnormal cavity formation that comes from the excessive conversion of cytoplasm to keratin (a strong protein that is the main substance that forms hair, skin, etc.) of epithelial cells, promoting detachment of tough cells and enhancing shedding. How to use REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL Apply REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL as advised by your physician. It is for external use only. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration for you depending on your age, body weight and disease condition. Side Effects Of REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL Common Skin irritation like redness, burning, stinging, dryness and peeling Rare Stop using REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL and contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following side effects: Excessive redness, swelling, blistering or crusting Allergic reaction (rash, hives or peeling skin with or without fever, wheezing, chest or throat tightness, trouble breathing, swallowing or talking, abnormal hoarseness, swelling of the mouth, face, lips, tongue or throat) Warning & Precautions Pregnancy REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL should be used in pregnant women only if specifically directed by your doctor. Consult your doctor before using it. Breastfeeding REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL should be used with caution in breastfeeding women. Consult your doctor before using it. Allergy Do not use REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL if you are allergic to Tretinoin or any of the other ingredients of this medicine. Others REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL is not recommended for use if you: Are sunburned Have eczema or other skin conditions Before applying REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL, inform your doctor if you: Have sun-sensitive skin Use in pediatrics: The safety and effectiveness of REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL in children (aged less than 12 years) have not been established. Consult your doctor before using it. Use in geriatrics: The safety and effectiveness of REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL in elderly patients (65 years and older) have not been established. Consult your doctor before using it. Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Before using REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines: Other medicines used to manage acne (Ex. benzoyl peroxide, resorcinol, salicylic acid) Medicated or abrasive soaps and cleansers Medicines containing high concentrations of alcohol, astringents or spices B. Drug-Food interactions: Avoid contact of the skin with the lime peel during management with REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL. Overdosage: If you or anyone else accidentally applied too much of REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL, contact your doctor immediately. Symptoms of overdose include irritation or increased irritation of your skin. Synopsis Drug : Tretinoin Pharmacological Category : Retinoids Therapeutic Indication : Acne Dosage Forms : Capsule, Cream, Gel, Gel (Topical) More Information Keep REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL out of reach of children Store below 25°C FAQs About REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL Q: Can the use of REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL manage wrinkles? A: REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL contains tretinoin, which is a derivative of vitamin A and is commonly used for various skin conditions, including acne and photoaging (skin aging caused by sun exposure). Tretinoin is known for its ability to stimulate collagen production and promote skin cell turnover, which can lead to improvements in skin texture and appearance. For wrinkles, tretinoin can be effective in reducing fine lines and improving skin elasticity. It works by increasing cell turnover and promoting the production of collagen, which can help to smooth out wrinkles over time. However, it does not completely manage wrinkles. Q: How long does it take for REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL to show results? A: Results from REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL, containing tretinoin, vary among individuals. Generally, noticeable improvements in skin texture and wrinkle reduction may take several weeks to months. In the initial 2-4 weeks, users may experience skin adjustment, potentially including redness or flakiness. Over the first 2-3 months, fine lines may begin to diminish as collagen production increases. Long-term and consistent use (3-6 months and beyond) is often necessary for the most significant improvements. Following dermatologist instructions and using sunscreen is crucial due to increased skin sensitivity. Individual responses differ, so patience is essential, and any concerns should be addressed with a dermatologist. Q: Can REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL remove dark spots? A: REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL containing tretinoin, can help reduce the appearance of dark spots by promoting skin cell turnover and inhibiting melanin production. While it may not completely manage dark spots, consistent and long-term use, along with sun protection, can lead to noticeable improvements. For a comprehensive approach, consulting with a dermatologist is recommended. Q: Can I use REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL daily? A: REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL should be used under careful medical supervision. Your doctor might recommend you to consistently use this medicine for a longer period of time to achieve best results. Following dermatologist instructions and using sunscreen is crucial due to increased skin sensitivity. It is important to stay with patience to notice results and if any concerns arise, kindly consult your doctor. Q: Does retinol brighten your skin? Yes, retinol is a vitamin A derivative with powerful antioxidant properties. It can contribute to skin brightening by promoting cell turnover and reducing hyperpigmentation, resulting in a more even complexion. Q: What is acne? Acne is a common skin condition characterized by the presence of pimples, blackheads, whiteheads, and inflammation, often caused by clogged hair follicles and the overproduction of oil. It is primarily caused by a combination of factors, including excess oil production, clogged hair follicles, bacteria (Propionibacterium acnes), and inflammation. Hormonal changes, genetics, certain medications, and lifestyle factors can also contribute to the development of acne. Q: What precautions should I take while using REVIZE MICRO 0.025% GEL? name: Persol Forte Cream 30gm
description: Introduction About PERSOL FORTE CREAM Persol Forte Cream is an antibacterial and anti-inflammatory gel, which is used for the management of acne vulgaris. It contains benzoyl peroxide and precipitated sulfur as active ingredients which kills the acne causing bacteria. Benzoyl Peroxide gets converted into benzoic acid which releases active free-radical oxygen. These free radicals interfere with important bacterial function and survival, hence killing them. It also increases the turnover rate of skin cells. Sulfur draws out oil from clogged pores and together they help in managing acne. Always apply Persol Forte Cream as advised by your physician. It is external use only. Wash the affected area with a mild cleanser pat your skin dry. Apply a thin layer over the affected area once or twice daily. If you have sensitive skin, apply once at night. Consult your doctor if you experience any allergic reactions while taking it. Key Composition Benzoyl Peroxide Precipitated Sulfur Therapeutic Uses Of PERSOL FORTE CREAM Manages acne vulgaris Side Effects Of PERSOL FORTE CREAM Persol Forte Cream may cause dry skin, skin redness, peeling of the skin, burning sensation of the skin, itching, pain, stinging, or skin irritation in some individuals. Consult your doctor if you notice any such side effects while applying Persol Forte Cream. Safety Advice Always apply Persol Forte Cream as advised by your physician It is for external use only Do not exceed the daily recommended dosage Wash the affected area with a mild cleanser pat your skin dry Apply a thin layer over the affected area once or twice daily If you have sensitive skin, apply once at night Do not use this gel if you are allergic to any of its components Persol Forte Cream is not recommended in pregnancy and breastfeeding women, unless considered necessary If your doctor advice you to use Persol Forte Cream during breastfeeding, it should not be applied to chest, as it may affect your child Avoid making contact with damaged skin, mouth, nose and mucous surfaces like the lining of your nose. If accidental contact occurs, thoroughly rinse with warm water Persol Forte Cream should not be used for children below 12 years of age Inform your doctor on all the medicines you use, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, as well as herbal supplements More Information Keep Persol Forte Cream out of the reach and sight of children Store at room temperature at below 25°C FAQs About PERSOL FORTE CREAM Q: What is Persol Forte Cream used for? A: Persol Forte Cream is an antibacterial and anti-inflammatory gel, which is used for the management of acne vulgaris. It contains benzoyl peroxide and precipitated sulfur as active ingredients which kills the acne causing bacteria. Q: How to you use Persol Forte Cream? A: Always apply Persol Forte Cream as advised by your physician. It is external use only. Wash the affected area with a mild cleanser pat your skin dry. Apply a thin layer over the affected area once or twice daily. If you have sensitive skin, apply once at night. Q: How long should I use Persol Forte Cream? A. Persol Forte Cream should be used for as long as it is recommended by your doctor. It might start showing up results by third week and reach its maximum efficiency in eight to twelve weeks. Do not use it for a prolonged period rather than as recommended by your doctor. Q: Can I use Persol Forte Cream if I have oily skin? A: Yes, you can use Persol Forte Cream even if you have oily skin. the ingredients of this cream pulls out excess oil from the skin ensuring that it doesn’t dry out your skin completely. Q. What precautions do I need to follow while using Persol Forte Cream? A. While you are using Persol Forte Cream, avoid unnecessary exposure to sun. You should always use sunscreens while using this product. It may cause swelling and blistering of the skin, if any of these symptoms occur, use of the Persol Forte Cream should be discontinued. Q: Can I leave Persol Forte Cream overnight? A: Yes. When you first start using Persol Forte Cream, it’s recommended to only leave the management on for a couple of hours for the first three days. This ensures that your skin is getting used to the active ingredient benzoyl peroxide. After three days of no redness, you can then apply this gel and leave it on overnight. Make sure to apply a moisturiser after this gel to manage any dryness from occurring. name: SOTRET NF 8 Capsule 10's
description: Introduction About SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE contains Isotretinoin, a retinoid medication specifically designed to manage severe acne in adults and children over 12 years of age. It is particularly effective for nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring when other anti-acne treatments have failed. Acne is a skin condition characterized by inflammatory spots, oily skin, and painful nodular lesions that commonly affect the face, chest, and back. Take SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE exactly as prescribed by your doctor, following the recommended dose and duration. It is best taken with food, preferably at the same time each day, to reduce the chances of missing a dose. It may take a few weeks before you notice an improvement in your symptoms but continue taking the medication as directed to achieve optimal results. If your condition does not improve after several weeks, consult your doctor for further advice. This medication can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, so limit sun exposure and use sunscreen when outdoors. It may also make your skin more fragile, so avoid waxing or laser treatments during therapy. Dryness of the lips, mouth, and eyes is another potential side effect—stay hydrated and use moisturizers or lubricating eye drops as needed Common side effects include dry skin, rashes, and elevated liver enzymes. While these are generally mild and tend to subside as your body adjusts to the medication, inform your doctor if they persist or cause discomfort. SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE is known to cause birth defects, so it should not be used during pregnancy or if you are planning to conceive. Always discuss your treatment plan with your doctor to ensure safety and effectiveness. Uses Of SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE Severe acne in adults and children (older than 12 years of age) Benefits of SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE for Acne: SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE is highly effective in managing severe acne conditions such as nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring. It works by reducing the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, unclogging pores, and decreasing inflammation, which helps to clear up existing acne and prevent new breakouts. This leads to smoother, healthier skin and reduces the risk of long-term scarring. Additionally, it targets the underlying causes of severe acne, making it a reliable choice for those who have not responded to other treatments. Always consult your doctor to ensure it is suitable for your condition. How SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE Works SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE work by targeting the root causes of severe acne. They reduce the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, which helps prevent pores from becoming clogged. This, in turn, reduces the growth of acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Isotretinoin also promotes the turnover of skin cells, preventing the formation of new acne lesions. Together, these actions help clear up existing acne and reduce the chances of scarring, making it an effective treatment for stubborn or severe acne conditions. How to use SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE Take SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the capsule whole with a glass of water; do not crush or chew it. It is recommended to take the capsule with food to improve absorption and reduce stomach discomfort. Take it at the same time each day to maintain consistent levels of the medication in your body. Follow the prescribed dosage and duration carefully. Do not stop the medication abruptly without consulting your doctor, even if your symptoms improve. Regular follow-ups and blood tests may be required to monitor your progress and ensure safe usage. Avoid alcohol, excessive sun exposure, and waxing or laser treatments during the treatment period. Use sunscreen and moisturizers as recommended by your doctor. What if I Forget to take SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose—do not double the dose to make up for it. Overdosage of SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE – In case you or anybody else accidently take too much of SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Symptoms of SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE overdose are severe headache, abdominal pain, nausea, dizziness, redness of face, vomiting, somnolence, irritability, and itching. Side Effects Of SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE Like all medicines SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE may cause certain side effects, although not everyone gets them Common Side Effects of SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE: Dry skin More fragile and red skin than usual, especially of the face Back, muscle or joint pain (particularly in children and teenagers) Raised liver enzymes Changed blood fat and cholesterol levels Easy bruising, bleeding or clotting Headache Protein or blood in the urine Becoming more prone to get infections Sore or inflamed throat and nose Stop taking SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE and consult your doctor immediately in case you experience any of the following: Persistent pain in your lower back or buttocks (signs of sacroiliitis) Severe skin reactions (Ex. erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis) (blistering and peeling of skin, severe rashes, fever, multiple lesions especially in mouth, nose, eyes and genitals, conjunctivitis, flu-like symptoms) Feeling depressed with suicidal thoughts Serious reactions (trouble breathing or swallowing due to sudden swelling of the throat, face, lips and mouth, sudden swelling of the hands, feet and ankles, hives, bruises, eczema, bruising, red patches on hands and legs) Rhabdomyolysis (muscle weakness along with trouble moving arms or legs, painful, swollen, bruised areas of the body, dark urine, reduced or no urination, confusion or dehydration) Hepatitis (yellow skin or eyes, tiredness) Kidney inflammation (difficulty urinating, swollen and puffy eyelids, excessive tiredness) How To Manage Side Effects Dry Skin Hydrate Regularly: Drink plenty of water throughout the day to keep your skin hydrated from within. Aim for at least 8–10 glasses daily. Use a Gentle Cleanser: Opt for a mild, fragrance-free cleanser to avoid further irritation. Avoid harsh soaps or scrubs that can strip the skin of natural oils. Moisturize Frequently: Apply a rich, non-comedogenic moisturizer to your face and body at least twice a day, especially after washing. Look for products with hydrating ingredients like hyaluronic acid or ceramides. Protect Your Lips: Use a moisturizing lip balm, preferably one with SPF, to prevent and treat cracked lips caused by dryness. Reapply as needed throughout the day. Avoid Long, Hot Showers: Hot water can strip your skin of its natural moisture. Take shorter showers with lukewarm water to minimize dryness. Humidify Your Environment: Use a humidifier in your home to add moisture to the air, especially during winter or in dry climates. Apply Sunscreen: Use a broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher daily to protect your sensitive skin from sun damage and prevent further dryness. Limit Exfoliation: Avoid physical or chemical exfoliants, as isotretinoin makes your skin more delicate and prone to irritation. Choose Gentle Fabrics: Wear soft, breathable fabrics like cotton to reduce friction and irritation on your dry skin. Seek Medical Advice: If dryness becomes severe or persistent despite home remedies, consult your doctor for additional treatment options or product recommendations. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy CONTRAINDICATED Human and animal studies have shown that isotretinoin is teratogenic in nature. Birth defects such as abnormalities of the face, eyes, ears, skull, central nervous system, cardiovascular system, and thymus and parathyroid glands or IQ less than score of 85 have been reported in female patients who were pregnant or became pregnant while on therapy with isotretinoin. Therefore, SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE is considered unsafe for use during pregnancy. Women of childbearing potential must use a reliable contraceptive method to avoid becoming pregnant. If you accidentally became pregnant while taking this medicine, stop taking it and consult your gynaecologist for further evaluation. It is also not recommended for you to get pregnant for one month after stopping isotretinoin tablets because some medicine may still be left in your body. Consult your doctor before taking it. Breastfeeding CONTRAINDICATED It is not known whether this medicine is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects, nursing mothers should not receive SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE Driving and Using Machines USE WITH CAUTION Do not drive or operate machinery if you experience dizziness, drowsiness or decreased night vision after taking SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE. Alcohol CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR Avoid consuming alcohol while taking SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE as it may increase side effects. Inform your doctor if you have an habit of chronic alcoholism. Kidney USE WITH CAUTION SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE should be used with caution in patients with kidney problems. Consult your doctor before taking it. Liver CONTRAINDICATED SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE is not recommended for use in patients with liver disease. Consult your doctor before taking it. Allergy CONTRAINDICATED Do not take SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE if you are allergic to Isotretinoin, soya, peanuts or any of the other ingredients of this medicine. Lungs USE WITH CAUTION SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE should be used with caution in patients having asthma. Consult your doctor before taking it. Use In Pediatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR The use of isotretinoin tablets in pediatric patients less than 12 years of age has not been studied. The use of isotretinoin for severe recalcitrant nodular acne in adolescents ages 12 to 17 years under careful medical supervision. Extreme caution should be taken if the child is suffering from metabolic or structural bone disease. Use In Geriatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR There is no proper information about the use of SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE in elderly patients. Consult your doctor before taking it. Others SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE is not recommended for use if you have: High blood fat levels High levels of Vitamin A Before taking SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE inform your doctor if you: Have or had mental illness or family history of mental illness such as depression, mood disorders, psychosis, aggressive behaviour, or hurting or killing self Have diabetes Are fructose intolerant Are overweight Safety Advice Always take isotretinoin with a meal to improve its absorption. Drink plenty of water to prevent dryness in your mouth and throat. Isotretinoin is related to vitamin A, so extra supplementation can cause toxicity. Avoid Excessive Sun Exposure: Wear sunscreen and protective clothing as isotretinoin can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Moisturize Regularly: Use lip balms and non-comedogenic moisturizers to manage dryness of lips and skin. Use Effective Birth Control: Isotretinoin can cause severe birth defects. Therefore, women must use reliable contraception as isotretinoin can cause severe birth defects. Do Not Donate Blood: Avoid donating blood while on isotretinoin and for at least a month after stopping it, as it can harm pregnant recipients. Follow Regular Check-Ups: Attend scheduled visits with your doctor for blood tests and monitoring. Avoid Waxing or Laser Treatments: Your skin is fragile during treatment and prone to scarring. Alcohol can increase the risk of liver problems, so limit or avoid it. Notify your doctor about severe dryness, mood changes, or unusual symptoms. Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Before taking SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines: Vitamin A supplements Medicines used to manage bacterial infections (Ex. minocycline, doxycycline) Phenytoin (used to manage fits) Medicines used to manage various inflammatory conditions (Ex. betamethasone, prednisolone, dexamethasone) Medicines used to manage pregnancy (Ex. Norethindrone, ethinyl Oestradiol) St. John’s wort (herbal medicine used to manage mental disorders) Other medicines used to manage acne like keratolytic or exfoliative agents (Ex. salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide) Synopsis Drug : Isotretinoin Pharmacological Category : Retinoids Therapeutic Indication : Severe acne Dosage Forms : Tablet, Soft gel Capsule, Capsule More Information Relevant Health Articles – Hormonal Acne: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment Anti-Acne Food: Eat Healthy To Heal Acne -Infographic FAQs About SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE Q: What is SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE used for? It works by reducing oil production in the skin and preventing clogged pores. Q: How should I take SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE? A: Take SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE as prescribed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily with food. Swallow the capsule whole with water, and avoid breaking or crushing it. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully for the best results. Q: What are the common side effects of SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE? A: Common side effects include dry skin, chapped lips, dry eyes, nosebleeds, and mild stomach discomfort. If you experience severe reactions like mood changes, persistent headaches, or vision problems, consult your doctor immediately. Q: Can SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE be taken during pregnancy? A: No, SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE should not be taken during pregnancy as it can cause severe birth defects. Women of childbearing age must use effective contraception during and at least one month after treatment. Q: Is SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE safe for long-term use? A: Isotretinoin is not usually prescribed for long-term use due to its potential side effects. Treatment duration is typically limited to 16–20 weeks. Always follow your doctor’s advice regarding treatment duration. Q: Can I use cosmetics while on SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE? A: Yes, you can use non-comedogenic and fragrance-free cosmetics. Avoid abrasive cleansers, harsh exfoliants, or acne products containing benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid, as these may irritate your skin. Q: Does SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE cause hair loss? A: Temporary hair thinning or hair loss can occur in some individuals during treatment. This side effect typically resolves after completing the course. If hair loss persists, consult your doctor. Q: Can I drink alcohol while taking SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE? A: It is advised to avoid alcohol while taking SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE, as it can increase the risk of liver damage and worsen side effects like dizziness or drowsiness. Be patient and continue using the medicine as prescribed. Q: What precautions should I take while using SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE? A: Avoid excessive sun exposure and use sunscreen. Can I play sports during SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE management? Consult your doctor if you can play sports during this management. Can I go out in the sun during SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE management? Sensitivity to light may increase during management with SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE so, avoid going too much into the sun and don’t use a sun-lamp or sun-bed. Before you go out in the sun, wear sunglasses and use sunscreen with a high protection factor (SPF 15 or higher). Can undergo cosmetic procedures while taking SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE? No. Do not undergo cosmetic procedures such as skin waxing, dermabrasion, laser, or artificial UV light detanning while taking SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE or at least for 6 months after stopping it as they could cause scarring, skin irritation, or changes in your skin colour. Consult your doctor before undergoing any cosmetic procedure while taking SOTRET NF 8 CAPSULE. References 1. KD Tripathi. Drugs Acting on Skin and Mucous Membranes. name: Adiff Aqueous Gel 15gm
description: FAQs About ADIFF GEL Q: Can ADIFF GEL be used in the morning? A: Apply ADIFF GEL as advised by your physician. It is best when applied at night and washed off in the morning since it is sensitive to sunlight. Consult your doctor for further queries. Q: Can ADIFF GEL cause skin irritation? A: ADIFF GEL may cause slight sensation of warmth and stinging after applying it for the initial 2-4 weeks. However, during the long-term usage this side effect usually disappears. Consult your doctor in case of any queries. Q: Can ADIFF GEL be used daily? A: In many cases, ADIFF GEL products are initially used once daily in the evening. However, some individuals may be advised to start with less frequent applications to allow the skin to adjust, and then gradually increase the frequency. Q: Can ADIFF GEL make skin darker? A: ADIFF GEL doesn’t make skin darker. Instead, it can slightly make the skin lighter by healing acne, pimples, blackheads and spots. Consult your doctor for further queries. Q: Can I go outside after applying ADIFF GEL? A: No, avoid going out after applying ADIFF GEL as it can cause local irritation and skin discomfort. It is best used at night. Consult the doctor for further assistance. Q: Can ADIFF GEL be used for other skin conditions? A: ADIFF GEL is primarily indicated for acne, but it may also be used off-label to manage other skin conditions such as keratosis pilaris (a common, harmless skin condition characterized by small, rough bumps on the skin). Q: Can ADIFF GEL be used with other acne medications? A: It's generally not recommended to use ADIFF GEL with other topical acne medications containing benzoyl peroxide, sulphur, resorcinol, or salicylic acid, as they may increase the risk of skin irritation. However, your healthcare provider may prescribe a combination regimen if deemed appropriate. Q: Can ADIFF GEL be applied under makeup or moisturizers? A: Yes, ADIFF GEL can be applied under makeup or moisturizers once it has been fully absorbed into the skin. It's important to allow the gel to dry completely before applying any other skincare products to avoid potential interactions or reduced effectiveness. Q: Can ADIFF GEL be used for acne scars? A: ADIFF GEL is primarily indicated for the management of acne lesions and may help improve the appearance of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (dark spots) caused by acne. However, it may have limited efficacy in managing deeper acne scars or pitted scars. Consult your healthcare provider for more information. Q: Can ADIFF GEL be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding? A: It's important to consult your healthcare provider before using ADIFF GEL if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. While topical retinoids are generally considered safe during pregnancy, it's best to discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. Author Details Written By Srilekha. R - B.Pharm Reviewed For Accuracy By Dr. Janet. C - Pharm.D Last updated on 19 Feb 2024 | 12:19 PM(IST)
