name: Bdiff A Gel 15gm
description: Introduction About BDIFF A GEL BDIFF A GEL is a combination of Adapalene and Benzoyl peroxide which belongs to the group of medicines called Antiacne agents. It is used in the management of acne. Acne vulgaris (commonly known as acne) is an inflammatory skin condition that occurs when the hair follicles present in the skin are clogged with excess oil and/or dead skin cells. It can also be aggravated by few bacteria (such as Propionibacterium acnes) and is highly common among on the teenagers and the young adults. It primarily affects the face, upper arms, trunk or back and is often characterized by pus-filled pimples, red bumps with inflammatory and non-inflammatory lesions. BDIFF A GEL is suitable for use both in adults and in children (aged 9 years or older). Apply a thin layer of BDIFF A GEL on the affected skin areas. Avoid contact of this medicine with your eyes, mouth, ears, nose or with open wounds. You must also protect your skin against sun light and against other light sources (such as UV lamps). Do not use BDIFF A GEL if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. BDIFF A GEL can be used in breastfeeding women if required. The most common side effects of using BDIFF A GEL are dry skin, mild burning sensation and skin irritation, redness or scaling. Consult your doctor if they trouble you. Uses Of BDIFF A GEL It is used in adults, children and in adolescents (aged 9 years or older) to: Manage acne How BDIFF A GEL Works BDIFF A GEL is a combination of two medicines namely, adapalene and benzoyl peroxide. Adapalene is a topical retinoid (a type of vitamin A). It modulates the skin cell cycle and manages the accumulation of excess sebum (natural oil produced by the skin) and dead skin cells on the hair follicles of the skin. It also reduces inflammation on the skin. Benzoyl peroxide is a keratolytic agent with antimicrobial properties. It improves skin’s tendency to exfoliate the dead skin cells naturally. It also reduces the number of acne-causing bacteria on the skin which can reduce the further spread of acne. Collectively, they unclog the hair follicles of the skin and exfoliates dead skin cells which reduces acne breakouts. How to use BDIFF A GEL Apply a thin layer of this medicine on the affected skin areas or as directed by the physician. It is for topical use only. Wash your hands before and after application. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and health condition. Avoid contact of BDIFF A GEL with your eyes, mouth, ears, nose, hair or with open wounds (cuts, scrapes or sunburn). Side Effects Of BDIFF A GEL Common Dry skin Skin redness and scaling Burning sensation of the skin Skin irritation Uncommon Itching of the skin (pruritus) Sunburn Rare Stop using BDIFF A GEL and consult your doctor immediately if you experience: Signs of allergic reaction (such as severe skin rash with itching of body parts, swelling of the eyes, face, lips or tongue causing throat tightness and breathing difficulties and feel faint) How To Manage Side Effects Skin redness and irritation: Place an icepack on the affected skin areas to ease the irritation. Avoid using harsh chemicals or soaps on the affected areas. Wear protective loose-fitting clothes while going outdoors. Regularly moisturize your skin. Avoid exposing your skin towards direct sunlight. If the condition did not improve, contact your doctor. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy BDIFF A GEL is not recommended for use in pregnant women. Therefore, inform your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. If you became pregnant while using this medicine, stop using it and contact your doctor immediately. Breastfeeding BDIFF A GEL can be used in breastfeeding women. However, do not apply this medicine on your chest to avoid exposing this medicine to the nursing infant. Allergy Talk to your doctor if you are allergic to Adapalene or Benzoyl peroxide. Others BDIFF A GEL is not recommended for use if you: Have any cuts, scrapes, sunburn or eczema at the site of application Use in Pediatrics: BDIFF A GEL can be used in children and adolescents (aged 9 years or older) if advised by the physician. Therefore, consult your doctor before using it. Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Before using BDIFF A GEL, inform your doctor if you are using any of the following: Other anti-acne medicines (such as clindamycin) Skin cosmetics (such as hair perming solutions, astringents, toners, shaving lotion, abrasive soaps or cleansers) Overdosage: If you or anyone else applied excessive amount of BDIFF A GEL, rinse your skin with plenty of cold water. If irritation persists, consult your doctor. Synopsis Drug : Adapalene, Benzoyl peroxide Pharmacological Category : Retinoid-like compounds, Topical Antibiotics Therapeutic Indication : Acne vulgaris Dosage Forms : Topical Gel More Information Keep BDIFF A GEL out of reach of children Store BDIFF A GEL at room temperature FAQs About BDIFF A GEL Will BDIFF A GEL be more effective if I overuse it? No. Do not overuse this medicine. If you use more, you will not get rid of acne quicker. Instead, it may make your skin more irritated and red. Therefore, only apply the quantity mentioned by your doctor. What are the side effects of using BDIFF A GEL? BDIFF A GEL is generally safe with limited or no side effects. However, you may experience skin dryness, redness or irritation after applying this medicine. Contact your doctor if it troubles you. What is the use of BDIFF A GEL? BDIFF A GEL is used in the management of acne. How BDIFF A GEL works? BDIFF A GEL manages the accumulation of excess sebum (natural oil produced by the skin) and dead skin cells on the hair follicles of the skin. It also reduces inflammation on the skin and improves skin’s tendency to exfoliate the dead skin cells naturally. It also reduces the number of acne-causing bacteria on the skin which can reduce the further spread of acne. How to use BDIFF A GEL? BDIFF A GEL is for external use only. Take the required quantity of the medicine and apply on the affected skin areas. Avoid contact of this medicine with your eyes, ears, nose or any other mucous membranes. How long does it take for BDIFF A GEL to work? It may take up to 2-3 weeks for BDIFF A GEL to show improvement in your skin condition. However, this period may vary from person-to-person depending upon the skin condition. How long should I use BDIFF A GEL? Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and health condition. You need to use BDIFF A GEL for the stipulated duration prescribed by your doctor. Failing to do so may not result in adequate response. What to do if I forgot to apply BDIFF A GEL? If you forgot to apply BDIFF A GEL, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is time for the next application, skip the missed one and apply the next dose. Do not excessively apply BDIFF A GEL to compensate the missed doses. Is BDIFF A GEL safe? BDIFF A GEL is safe at doses prescribed by the physician. Therefore, do not alter the dose of BDIFF A GEL without consulting your doctor. Can I stop using BDIFF A GEL without consulting your doctor? No. You should not stop using BDIFF A GEL without consulting your doctor as it may reduce its effectiveness. Therefore, apply BDIFF A GEL for the stipulated duration recommended by your doctor to achieve maximum results. Can BDIFF A GEL be used in pregnant women? BDIFF A GEL is not recommended for use in pregnant women. Therefore, inform your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. name: Isotane 20mg Capsule 10'S
description: Introduction About ISOTANE 20MG CAPSULE ISOTANE 20MG CAPSULE contains Isotretinoin, a retinoid medication specifically designed to manage severe acne in adults and children over 12 years of age. It is particularly effective for nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring when other anti-acne treatments have failed. Acne is a skin condition characterized by inflammatory spots, oily skin, and painful nodular lesions that commonly affect the face, chest, and back. Take ISOTANE 20MG CAPSULE exactly as prescribed by your doctor, following the recommended dose and duration. It is best taken with food, preferably at the same time each day, to reduce the chances of missing a dose. It may take a few weeks before you notice an improvement in your symptoms but continue taking the medication as directed to achieve optimal results. If your condition does not improve after several weeks, consult your doctor for further advice. This medication can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, so limit sun exposure and use sunscreen when outdoors. It may also make your skin more fragile, so avoid waxing or laser treatments during therapy. Dryness of the lips, mouth, and eyes is another potential side effect—stay hydrated and use moisturizers or lubricating eye drops as needed Common side effects include dry skin, rashes, and elevated liver enzymes. While these are generally mild and tend to subside as your body adjusts to the medication, inform your doctor if they persist or cause discomfort. ISOTANE 20MG CAPSULE is known to cause birth defects, so it should not be used during pregnancy or if you are planning to conceive. Always discuss your treatment plan with your doctor to ensure safety and effectiveness. Uses Of ISOTANE 20MG CAPSULE Severe acne in adults and children (older than 12 years of age) Benefits of ISOTANE 20MG CAPSULE for Acne: ISOTANE 20MG CAPSULE is highly effective in managing severe acne conditions such as nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring. It works by reducing the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, unclogging pores, and decreasing inflammation, which helps to clear up existing acne and prevent new breakouts. This leads to smoother, healthier skin and reduces the risk of long-term scarring. Additionally, it targets the underlying causes of severe acne, making it a reliable choice for those who have not responded to other treatments. Always consult your doctor to ensure it is suitable for your condition. How ISOTANE 20MG CAPSULE Works ISOTANE 20MG CAPSULE work by targeting the root causes of severe acne. They reduce the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, which helps prevent pores from becoming clogged. This, in turn, reduces the growth of acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Isotretinoin also promotes the turnover of skin cells, preventing the formation of new acne lesions. Together, these actions help clear up existing acne and reduce the chances of scarring, making it an effective treatment for stubborn or severe acne conditions. How to use ISOTANE 20MG CAPSULE Take ISOTANE 20MG CAPSULE exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the capsule whole with a glass of water; do not crush or chew it. It is recommended to take the capsule with food to improve absorption and reduce stomach discomfort. Take it at the same time each day to maintain consistent levels of the medication in your body. Follow the prescribed dosage and duration carefully. Do not stop the medication abruptly without consulting your doctor, even if your symptoms improve. Regular follow-ups and blood tests may be required to monitor your progress and ensure safe usage. Avoid alcohol, excessive sun exposure, and waxing or laser treatments during the treatment period. Use sunscreen and moisturizers as recommended by your doctor. What if I Forget to take ISOTANE 20MG CAPSULE: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose—do not double the dose to make up for it. name: SAFERET 10 Tablet 10's
description: Introduction About SAFERET 10 TABLET SAFERET 10 TABLET contains Isotretinoin, a retinoid medication specifically designed to manage severe acne in adults and children over 12 years of age. It is particularly effective for nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring when other anti-acne treatments have failed. Acne is a skin condition characterized by inflammatory spots, oily skin, and painful nodular lesions that commonly affect the face, chest, and back. Take SAFERET 10 TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor, following the recommended dose and duration. It is best taken with food, preferably at the same time each day, to reduce the chances of missing a dose. It may take a few weeks before you notice an improvement in your symptoms but continue taking the medication as directed to achieve optimal results. If your condition does not improve after several weeks, consult your doctor for further advice. This medication can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, so limit sun exposure and use sunscreen when outdoors. It may also make your skin more fragile, so avoid waxing or laser treatments during therapy. Dryness of the lips, mouth, and eyes is another potential side effect—stay hydrated and use moisturizers or lubricating eye drops as needed Common side effects include dry skin, rashes, and elevated liver enzymes. While these are generally mild and tend to subside as your body adjusts to the medication, inform your doctor if they persist or cause discomfort. SAFERET 10 TABLET is known to cause birth defects, so it should not be used during pregnancy or if you are planning to conceive. Always discuss your treatment plan with your doctor to ensure safety and effectiveness. Uses Of SAFERET 10 TABLET Severe acne in adults and children (older than 12 years of age) Benefits of SAFERET 10 TABLET for Acne: SAFERET 10 TABLET is highly effective in managing severe acne conditions such as nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring. It works by reducing the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, unclogging pores, and decreasing inflammation, which helps to clear up existing acne and prevent new breakouts. This leads to smoother, healthier skin and reduces the risk of long-term scarring. Additionally, it targets the underlying causes of severe acne, making it a reliable choice for those who have not responded to other treatments. Always consult your doctor to ensure it is suitable for your condition. How SAFERET 10 TABLET Works SAFERET 10 TABLET work by targeting the root causes of severe acne. They reduce the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, which helps prevent pores from becoming clogged. This, in turn, reduces the growth of acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Isotretinoin also promotes the turnover of skin cells, preventing the formation of new acne lesions. Together, these actions help clear up existing acne and reduce the chances of scarring, making it an effective treatment for stubborn or severe acne conditions. How to use SAFERET 10 TABLET Take SAFERET 10 TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the capsule whole with a glass of water; do not crush or chew it. It is recommended to take the capsule with food to improve absorption and reduce stomach discomfort. Take it at the same time each day to maintain consistent levels of the medication in your body. Follow the prescribed dosage and duration carefully. Do not stop the medication abruptly without consulting your doctor, even if your symptoms improve. Regular follow-ups and blood tests may be required to monitor your progress and ensure safe usage. Avoid alcohol, excessive sun exposure, and waxing or laser treatments during the treatment period. Use sunscreen and moisturizers as recommended by your doctor. What if I Forget to take SAFERET 10 TABLET: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose—do not double the dose to make up for it. Overdosage of SAFERET 10 TABLET – In case you or anybody else accidently take too much of SAFERET 10 TABLET, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Symptoms of SAFERET 10 TABLET overdose are severe headache, abdominal pain, nausea, dizziness, redness of face, vomiting, somnolence, irritability, and itching. Side Effects Of SAFERET 10 TABLET Like all medicines SAFERET 10 TABLET may cause certain side effects, although not everyone gets them Common Side Effects of SAFERET 10 TABLET: Dry skin More fragile and red skin than usual, especially of the face Back, muscle or joint pain (particularly in children and teenagers) Raised liver enzymes Changed blood fat and cholesterol levels Easy bruising, bleeding or clotting Headache Protein or blood in the urine Becoming more prone to get infections Sore or inflamed throat and nose Stop taking SAFERET 10 TABLET and consult your doctor immediately in case you experience any of the following: Persistent pain in your lower back or buttocks (signs of sacroiliitis) Severe skin reactions (Ex. erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis) (blistering and peeling of skin, severe rashes, fever, multiple lesions especially in mouth, nose, eyes and genitals, conjunctivitis, flu-like symptoms) Feeling depressed with suicidal thoughts Serious reactions (trouble breathing or swallowing due to sudden swelling of the throat, face, lips and mouth, sudden swelling of the hands, feet and ankles, hives, bruises, eczema, bruising, red patches on hands and legs) Rhabdomyolysis (muscle weakness along with trouble moving arms or legs, painful, swollen, bruised areas of the body, dark urine, reduced or no urination, confusion or dehydration) Hepatitis (yellow skin or eyes, tiredness) Kidney inflammation (difficulty urinating, swollen and puffy eyelids, excessive tiredness) How To Manage Side Effects Dry Skin Hydrate Regularly: Drink plenty of water throughout the day to keep your skin hydrated from within. Aim for at least 8–10 glasses daily. Use a Gentle Cleanser: Opt for a mild, fragrance-free cleanser to avoid further irritation. Avoid harsh soaps or scrubs that can strip the skin of natural oils. Moisturize Frequently: Apply a rich, non-comedogenic moisturizer to your face and body at least twice a day, especially after washing. Look for products with hydrating ingredients like hyaluronic acid or ceramides. Protect Your Lips: Use a moisturizing lip balm, preferably one with SPF, to prevent and treat cracked lips caused by dryness. Reapply as needed throughout the day. Avoid Long, Hot Showers: Hot water can strip your skin of its natural moisture. Take shorter showers with lukewarm water to minimize dryness. Humidify Your Environment: Use a humidifier in your home to add moisture to the air, especially during winter or in dry climates. Apply Sunscreen: Use a broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher daily to protect your sensitive skin from sun damage and prevent further dryness. Limit Exfoliation: Avoid physical or chemical exfoliants, as isotretinoin makes your skin more delicate and prone to irritation. Choose Gentle Fabrics: Wear soft, breathable fabrics like cotton to reduce friction and irritation on your dry skin. Seek Medical Advice: If dryness becomes severe or persistent despite home remedies, consult your doctor for additional treatment options or product recommendations. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy CONTRAINDICATED Human and animal studies have shown that isotretinoin is teratogenic in nature. Birth defects such as abnormalities of the face, eyes, ears, skull, central nervous system, cardiovascular system, and thymus and parathyroid glands or IQ less than score of 85 have been reported in female patients who were pregnant or became pregnant while on therapy with isotretinoin. Therefore, SAFERET 10 TABLET is considered unsafe for use during pregnancy. Women of childbearing potential must use a reliable contraceptive method to avoid becoming pregnant. If you accidentally became pregnant while taking this medicine, stop taking it and consult your gynaecologist for further evaluation. It is also not recommended for you to get pregnant for one month after stopping isotretinoin tablets because some medicine may still be left in your body. Consult your doctor before taking it. Breastfeeding CONTRAINDICATED It is not known whether this medicine is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects, nursing mothers should not receive SAFERET 10 TABLET Driving and Using Machines USE WITH CAUTION Do not drive or operate machinery if you experience dizziness, drowsiness or decreased night vision after taking SAFERET 10 TABLET. Alcohol CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR Avoid consuming alcohol while taking SAFERET 10 TABLET as it may increase side effects. Inform your doctor if you have an habit of chronic alcoholism. Kidney USE WITH CAUTION SAFERET 10 TABLET should be used with caution in patients with kidney problems. Consult your doctor before taking it. Liver CONTRAINDICATED SAFERET 10 TABLET is not recommended for use in patients with liver disease. Consult your doctor before taking it. Allergy CONTRAINDICATED Do not take SAFERET 10 TABLET if you are allergic to Isotretinoin, soya, peanuts or any of the other ingredients of this medicine. Lungs USE WITH CAUTION SAFERET 10 TABLET should be used with caution in patients having asthma. Consult your doctor before taking it. Use In Pediatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR The use of isotretinoin tablets in pediatric patients less than 12 years of age has not been studied. The use of isotretinoin for severe recalcitrant nodular acne in adolescents ages 12 to 17 years under careful medical supervision. Extreme caution should be taken if the child is suffering from metabolic or structural bone disease. Use In Geriatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR There is no proper information about the use of SAFERET 10 TABLET in elderly patients. Consult your doctor before taking it. Others SAFERET 10 TABLET is not recommended for use if you have: High blood fat levels High levels of Vitamin A Before taking SAFERET 10 TABLET inform your doctor if you: Have or had mental illness or family history of mental illness such as depression, mood disorders, psychosis, aggressive behaviour, or hurting or killing self Have diabetes Are fructose intolerant Are overweight Safety Advice Always take isotretinoin with a meal to improve its absorption. Drink plenty of water to prevent dryness in your mouth and throat. Isotretinoin is related to vitamin A, so extra supplementation can cause toxicity. Avoid Excessive Sun Exposure: Wear sunscreen and protective clothing as isotretinoin can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Moisturize Regularly: Use lip balms and non-comedogenic moisturizers to manage dryness of lips and skin. Use Effective Birth Control: Isotretinoin can cause severe birth defects. Therefore, women must use reliable contraception as isotretinoin can cause severe birth defects. Do Not Donate Blood: Avoid donating blood while on isotretinoin and for at least a month after stopping it, as it can harm pregnant recipients. Follow Regular Check-Ups: Attend scheduled visits with your doctor for blood tests and monitoring. Avoid Waxing or Laser Treatments: Your skin is fragile during treatment and prone to scarring. Alcohol can increase the risk of liver problems, so limit or avoid it. Notify your doctor about severe dryness, mood changes, or unusual symptoms. Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Before taking SAFERET 10 TABLET, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines: Vitamin A supplements Medicines used to manage bacterial infections (Ex. minocycline, doxycycline) Phenytoin (used to manage fits) Medicines used to manage various inflammatory conditions (Ex. betamethasone, prednisolone, dexamethasone) Medicines used to manage pregnancy (Ex. Norethindrone, ethinyl Oestradiol) St. John’s wort (herbal medicine used to manage mental disorders) Other medicines used to manage acne like keratolytic or exfoliative agents (Ex. salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide) Synopsis Drug : Isotretinoin Pharmacological Category : Retinoids Therapeutic Indication : Severe acne Dosage Forms : Tablet, Soft gel Capsule, Capsule More Information Relevant Health Articles – Hormonal Acne: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment Anti-Acne Food: Eat Healthy To Heal Acne -Infographic FAQs About SAFERET 10 TABLET Q: What is SAFERET 10 TABLET used for? A: SAFERET 10 TABLET is used to manage severe acne (nodular or cystic acne) that does not respond to other treatments like antibiotics. It works by reducing oil production in the skin and preventing clogged pores. Q: How should I take SAFERET 10 TABLET? A: Take SAFERET 10 TABLET as prescribed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily with food. Swallow the capsule whole with water, and avoid breaking or crushing it. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully for the best results. Q: What are the common side effects of SAFERET 10 TABLET? A: Common side effects include dry skin, chapped lips, dry eyes, nosebleeds, and mild stomach discomfort. If you experience severe reactions like mood changes, persistent headaches, or vision problems, consult your doctor immediately. Q: Can SAFERET 10 TABLET be taken during pregnancy? A: No, SAFERET 10 TABLET should not be taken during pregnancy as it can cause severe birth defects. Women of childbearing age must use effective contraception during and at least one month after treatment. Q: Is SAFERET 10 TABLET safe for long-term use? A: Isotretinoin is not usually prescribed for long-term use due to its potential side effects. Treatment duration is typically limited to 16–20 weeks. Always follow your doctor’s advice regarding treatment duration. Q: Can I use cosmetics while on SAFERET 10 TABLET? A: Yes, you can use non-comedogenic and fragrance-free cosmetics. Avoid abrasive cleansers, harsh exfoliants, or acne products containing benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid, as these may irritate your skin. Q: Does SAFERET 10 TABLET cause hair loss? A: Temporary hair thinning or hair loss can occur in some individuals during treatment. This side effect typically resolves after completing the course. If hair loss persists, consult your doctor. Q: Can I drink alcohol while taking SAFERET 10 TABLET? A: It is advised to avoid alcohol while taking SAFERET 10 TABLET, as it can increase the risk of liver damage and worsen side effects like dizziness or drowsiness. Q: How long does it take for SAFERET 10 TABLET to work? A: You may start noticing improvements within 4–8 weeks, but the full effects are usually seen after completing the treatment course. Be patient and continue using the medicine as prescribed. Q: What precautions should I take while using SAFERET 10 TABLET? A: Avoid excessive sun exposure and use sunscreen. Do not donate blood during and for one month after treatment. Inform your doctor about any other medications or supplements you are taking. Use a reliable birth control to avoid becoming pregnant while taking SAFERET 10 TABLET. Do not undergo cosmetic procedures such as skin waxing, dermabrasion, laser, or artificial UV light detanning while taking SAFERET 10 TABLET without consulting your doctor. Q: Can SAFERET 10 TABLET be used by men? A: Yes, SAFERET 10 TABLET is safe for men to use for severe acne. However, male patients planning to father a child need not take special precautions, as isotretinoin does not affect sperm. Can SAFERET 10 TABLET cause irregular periods? According to some studies, menstrual irregularity was observed during management follow-ups. Consult your doctor if you experience irregularity in your periods during management with SAFERET 10 TABLET. Is SAFERET 10 TABLET safe to take in pregnancy? No. SAFERET 10 TABLET is not recommended for use in pregnant women and women planning a pregnancy. Inform your doctor if you become pregnant during management with SAFERET 10 TABLET. It is not recommended to get pregnant for one month after stopping SAFERET 10 TABLET management because some medicine may still be left in your body. Consult your doctor before taking it. Contraception must be used for a month before taking SAFERET 10 TABLET, during management and for a month afterwards. Discuss with your doctor regarding suitable contraceptive methods. Consult your doctor if you can play sports during this management. Can I go out in the sun during SAFERET 10 TABLET management? Sensitivity to light may increase during management with SAFERET 10 TABLET so, avoid going too much into the sun and don’t use a sun-lamp or sun-bed. name: Peroduo Gel 15gm
description: Introduction About PERODUO GEL PERODUO GEL is a combination of Adapalene and Benzoyl peroxide which belongs to the group of medicines called Antiacne agents. It is used in the management of acne. Acne vulgaris (commonly known as acne) is an inflammatory skin condition that occurs when the hair follicles present in the skin are clogged with excess oil and/or dead skin cells. It can also be aggravated by few bacteria (such as Propionibacterium acnes) and is highly common among on the teenagers and the young adults. It primarily affects the face, upper arms, trunk or back and is often characterized by pus-filled pimples, red bumps with inflammatory and non-inflammatory lesions. PERODUO GEL is suitable for use both in adults and in children (aged 9 years or older). Apply a thin layer of PERODUO GEL on the affected skin areas. Avoid contact of this medicine with your eyes, mouth, ears, nose or with open wounds. You must also protect your skin against sun light and against other light sources (such as UV lamps). Do not use PERODUO GEL if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. PERODUO GEL can be used in breastfeeding women if required. The most common side effects of using PERODUO GEL are dry skin, mild burning sensation and skin irritation, redness or scaling. Consult your doctor if they trouble you. Uses Of PERODUO GEL It is used in adults, children and in adolescents (aged 9 years or older) to: Manage acne How PERODUO GEL Works PERODUO GEL is a combination of two medicines namely, adapalene and benzoyl peroxide. Adapalene is a topical retinoid (a type of vitamin A). It modulates the skin cell cycle and manages the accumulation of excess sebum (natural oil produced by the skin) and dead skin cells on the hair follicles of the skin. It also reduces inflammation on the skin. Benzoyl peroxide is a keratolytic agent with antimicrobial properties. It improves skin’s tendency to exfoliate the dead skin cells naturally. It also reduces the number of acne-causing bacteria on the skin which can reduce the further spread of acne. Collectively, they unclog the hair follicles of the skin and exfoliates dead skin cells which reduces acne breakouts. How to use PERODUO GEL Apply a thin layer of this medicine on the affected skin areas or as directed by the physician. It is for topical use only. Wash your hands before and after application. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and health condition. Avoid contact of PERODUO GEL with your eyes, mouth, ears, nose, hair or with open wounds (cuts, scrapes or sunburn). Side Effects Of PERODUO GEL Common Dry skin Skin redness and scaling Burning sensation of the skin Skin irritation Uncommon Itching of the skin (pruritus) Sunburn Rare Stop using PERODUO GEL and consult your doctor immediately if you experience: Signs of allergic reaction (such as severe skin rash with itching of body parts, swelling of the eyes, face, lips or tongue causing throat tightness and breathing difficulties and feel faint) How To Manage Side Effects Skin redness and irritation: Place an icepack on the affected skin areas to ease the irritation. Avoid using harsh chemicals or soaps on the affected areas. Wear protective loose-fitting clothes while going outdoors. Regularly moisturize your skin. Avoid exposing your skin towards direct sunlight. If the condition did not improve, contact your doctor. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy PERODUO GEL is not recommended for use in pregnant women. Therefore, inform your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. If you became pregnant while using this medicine, stop using it and contact your doctor immediately. Breastfeeding PERODUO GEL can be used in breastfeeding women. However, do not apply this medicine on your chest to avoid exposing this medicine to the nursing infant. Allergy Talk to your doctor if you are allergic to Adapalene or Benzoyl peroxide. Others PERODUO GEL is not recommended for use if you: Have any cuts, scrapes, sunburn or eczema at the site of application Use in Pediatrics: PERODUO GEL can be used in children and adolescents (aged 9 years or older) if advised by the physician. Therefore, consult your doctor before using it. Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Before using PERODUO GEL, inform your doctor if you are using any of the following: Other anti-acne medicines (such as clindamycin) Skin cosmetics (such as hair perming solutions, astringents, toners, shaving lotion, abrasive soaps or cleansers) Overdosage: If you or anyone else applied excessive amount of PERODUO GEL, rinse your skin with plenty of cold water. If irritation persists, consult your doctor. Synopsis Drug : Adapalene, Benzoyl peroxide Pharmacological Category : Retinoid-like compounds, Topical Antibiotics Therapeutic Indication : Acne vulgaris Dosage Forms : Topical Gel More Information Keep PERODUO GEL out of reach of children Store PERODUO GEL at room temperature FAQs About PERODUO GEL Will PERODUO GEL be more effective if I overuse it? No. Do not overuse this medicine. If you use more, you will not get rid of acne quicker. Instead, it may make your skin more irritated and red. Therefore, only apply the quantity mentioned by your doctor. What are the side effects of using PERODUO GEL? PERODUO GEL is generally safe with limited or no side effects. However, you may experience skin dryness, redness or irritation after applying this medicine. Contact your doctor if it troubles you. What is the use of PERODUO GEL? PERODUO GEL is used in the management of acne. How PERODUO GEL works? PERODUO GEL manages the accumulation of excess sebum (natural oil produced by the skin) and dead skin cells on the hair follicles of the skin. It also reduces inflammation on the skin and improves skin’s tendency to exfoliate the dead skin cells naturally. It also reduces the number of acne-causing bacteria on the skin which can reduce the further spread of acne. How to use PERODUO GEL? PERODUO GEL is for external use only. Take the required quantity of the medicine and apply on the affected skin areas. Avoid contact of this medicine with your eyes, ears, nose or any other mucous membranes. How long does it take for PERODUO GEL to work? It may take up to 2-3 weeks for PERODUO GEL to show improvement in your skin condition. However, this period may vary from person-to-person depending upon the skin condition. How long should I use PERODUO GEL? Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and health condition. No. You should not stop using PERODUO GEL without consulting your doctor as it may reduce its effectiveness. Therefore, apply PERODUO GEL for the stipulated duration recommended by your doctor to achieve maximum results. Can PERODUO GEL be used in pregnant women? PERODUO GEL is not recommended for use in pregnant women. Therefore, inform your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. Therefore, do not alter the dose of PERODUO GEL without consulting your doctor. Can I stop using PERODUO GEL without consulting your doctor? PERODUO GEL is not recommended for use in pregnant women. Therefore, inform your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. name: Femcinol A Gel 20gm
description: Introduction About FEMCINOL A GEL FEMCINOL A GEL is a combination of Clindamycin and Nicotinamide which belongs to a group of medicines called Lincomycin antibiotics and Vitamin B3 complex, respectively. FEMCINOL A GEL is used to manage mild to moderate acne which is a skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells which may occur due to variety of causes such as genetics, fluctuating hormone levels, stress, high humidity or using oily or greasy personal care products which may affect people of all ages. It is characterized by symptoms such as open or closed plugged pores, small red & tender bumps, pimples, large, solid or painful lumps under the skin and painful & pus-filled lumps under the skin. Before using FEMCINOL A GEL inform your doctor if you have liver, kidney, lung or heart diseases. Avoid applying FEMCINOL A GEL to a cut, scrapped, sunburnt or eczema affected skin. FEMCINOL A GEL should be used with caution in pregnant and in breastfeeding women. FEMCINOL A GEL is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (below 12 years). Consult your doctor before applying. The most common side effects of using FEMCINOL A GEL are skin inflammation, contact dermatitis (red, itchy rash), inflammation of hair follicles, itchy skin, dry skin and peeling of skin. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsen. Uses Of FEMCINOL A GEL Manage mild to moderate acne How FEMCINOL A GEL Works FEMCINOL A GEL helps to manage acne, where Clindamycin reduces free fatty acid concentrations on the skin and suppresses the growth of Propionibacterium acnes (Corynebacterium acnes), a bacteria found in sebaceous glands and follicles and Nicotinamide exerts anti-inflammatory effect in acne and interrupts sebum production. How to use FEMCINOL A GEL Apply FEMCINOL A GEL as advised by your physician. It is for external use only. Before applying the medicine normally wash and dry the affected area and apply a thin layer of this medicine on the affected area. Managed areas on the face need not be covered with a plaster or bandage. Do not apply this medicine beyond the recommended duration. Avoid applying FEMCINOL A GEL around your eyes, including eyelids. Rinse it off with water if you accidentally get it in these areas. Side Effects Of FEMCINOL A GEL Common Contact dermatitis (red, itchy rash) Inflammation of hair follicles Itchy skin Dry skin Peeling of skin How To Manage Side Effects Skin rash/Itchy skin: Avoid hot bath because hot water can irritate your skin further. Do not scratch the affected area. Use protective clothing when going outdoors. Regularly moisturize your skin and apply calamine lotion as a coolant. Discuss with your doctor if the symptom worsens. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy FEMCINOL A GEL should be used with caution in pregnant women. Consult your doctor before applying. Breastfeeding FEMCINOL A GEL should be used with caution in breastfeeding women. Consult your doctor before applying. Allergy FEMCINOL A GEL is not recommended for use if you are allergic to Clindamycin, Nicotinamide or any other ingredients of this medicine. Others FEMCINOL A GEL is not recommended for use if you have: Eczema (skin inflammation) Cut, scrapped, sunburnt skin Use in Pediatrics: FEMCINOL A GEL is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (below 12 years). Consult your doctor before using it for your child. Use in Geriatrics: There is no information on the use of FEMCINOL A GEL in elderly patients. Consult with your doctor before using. Interactions A. Drug - Drug interactions: Before using FEMCINOL A GEL, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines: Acepromazine (used a sedative/tranquilizer) Acetaminophen (used to manage pain and inflammation) Overdosage: If you or anyone else accidentally ingests or applies too much of FEMCINOL A GEL, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Before using FEMCINOL A GEL inform your doctor if you have liver, kidney, lung or heart diseases. Avoid applying FEMCINOL A GEL to a cut, scrapped, sunburnt or eczema affected skin. FEMCINOL A GEL is indicated for the management of mild to moderate acne in patients above 12 years of age. Do not use it for any other condition other than that prescribed by your doctor. How should I use FEMCINOL A GEL? Always apply FEMCINOL A GEL, as directed by your physician. It is for external use only. On the affected area, apply a thin layer of this medicine. Managed areas on the face need not be covered with a plaster or bandage. Do not apply this medicine on your face beyond 5 days. Avoid applying FEMCINOL A GEL around your eyes, including eyelids. Avoid hot bath because hot water can irritate your skin further. Do not scratch the affected area. Use protective clothing when going outdoors. name: Ezanic 20% Gel 15gm
description: Introduction About EZANIC 20% GEL EZANIC 20% GEL contains Azelaic acid which belongs to the group of medicines called Dicarboxylic acids. It is used to manage common acne (acne vulgaris). It is also used for the management of mild to moderate papulopustular rosacea. Acne is a skin condition that occurs when the hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells. It causes whiteheads, blackheads or pimples. Rosacea is a skin condition that causes blushing or redness, pus-filled bumps and small visible blood vessels in the face. EZANIC 20% GEL should be applied with caution in patients with lung problems such as asthma. Consult your doctor before applying it. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before applying this medicine. Your doctor will decide whether you can use this medicine. EZANIC 20% GEL is generally not recommended for use in children under 12 years of age for the management of acne and also not recommended for use in children under 18 years of age for the management of rosacea. Consult your doctor before applying it. The most common side effects of applying EZANIC 20% GEL are burning, itching or redness of the skin (erythema) at the application site, scaling, pain, dryness, skin discolouration or irritation at the application site. Contact your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen. Uses Of EZANIC 20% GEL Common acne (acne vulgaris) Mild to moderate papulopustular rosacea How EZANIC 20% GEL Works EZANIC 20% GEL attacks the bacteria called propionibacterium acnes, which plays an essential part in causing acne. It also reduces growth of the harder outermost skin cells (keratin surface cells) that block the pores of the skin to cause blackheads and whiteheads. How to use EZANIC 20% GEL Apply EZANIC 20% GEL as directed by your physician. It is for external use only. Wash your hands with soap and water before and after using EZANIC 20% GEL. Apply a thin layer of this medicine on the affected area and rub it gently into the skin. Avoid applying this medicine around your eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes or open wounds. If it does, wash the eyes, mouth or other mucous membranes immediately with large amounts of cool water. Side Effects Of EZANIC 20% GEL Common Burning, itching or redness of the skin (erythema) at the application site Scaling, pain, dryness, skin discolouration or irritation at the application site Uncommon Greasy skin Acne or loss of skin colour Tingling Dermatitis Discomfort or swelling at the application site Rare Cracking of the lips, small blisters Eczema, ulceration Warmth at the site of application Allergic reaction such as urticaria or hives, rash at the site of application Worsening of asthma Stop applying EZANIC 20% GEL and contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following side effects: Allergic reaction such as rash, angioedema (swelling under the skin), swelling of face, eyes and dyspnoea (shortness of breath) How To Manage Side Effects Skin rash: Avoid hot bath because hot water can irritate your skin further. Do not scratch the affected area. Use sunscreen and wear protective clothing while going outside. Use unscented moisturizers to soothe and hydrate the affected area. Contact your doctor if the rashes worsen. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or are planning to have a baby before applying this medicine. Your doctor will decide whether you can use EZANIC 20% GEL. Breastfeeding EZANIC 20% GEL should be used with caution in breastfeeding women. Consult your doctor before applying it. Infants must not come into contact with managed skin or breasts. Driving and Using Machines EZANIC 20% GEL has no influence on the ability to drive and use machines. Allergy Do not apply EZANIC 20% GEL if you are allergic to Azelaic acid or any of the other ingredients of this medicine. Lungs EZANIC 20% GEL should be applied with caution in patients with lung problems such as asthma. Consult your doctor before applying it. Others Use in pediatrics: EZANIC 20% GEL is generally not recommended for use in children under 12 years of age for the management of acne. It is also not recommended for use in children under 18 years of age for the management of rosacea due to a lack of data on safety and efficacy. Consult your doctor before applying it. Use in geriatrics: There is limited information available on the use of EZANIC 20% GEL in elderly patients. Consult your doctor before applying it. Interactions A. Drug - Drug interactions: Tell your doctor if you are taking or have recently taken any other medicines, including medicines obtained without a prescription, vitamin supplement or herbal products. Overdosage: If you or anyone else accidentally used too much of EZANIC 20% GEL or if you or a child accidentally swallow the medicine, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Synopsis Drug : Azelaic acid Pharmacological Category : Dicarboxylic acids Therapeutic Indication : Common acne, Papulopustular rosacea Dosage Forms : Cream, Gel, Gel (Topical) More Information Keep EZANIC 20% GEL out of the sight and reach of children Store EZANIC 20% GEL below 30°C FAQs About EZANIC 20% GEL How long can I use EZANIC 20% GEL? How long EZANIC 20% GEL has to be used varies from person to person. It depends upon how bad your acne is when you start management. In general, you may notice a distinct improvement after 4 weeks. In case of no improvement after 1 month or if the acne or rosacea becomes worse, you should discontinue EZANIC 20% GEL and consult your doctor. How long does it take EZANIC 20% GEL to lighten skin? EZANIC 20% GEL when applied twice daily for several (up to 8 months), skin lightening starts after 1 to 2 months of using it. But when EZANIC 20% GEL is used in combination with a medicine called tretinoin causes more skin lightening after 3 months than EZANIC 20% GEL alone. Consult your doctor for advice. Can I use EZANIC 20% GEL for hair growth? Yes. EZANIC 20% GEL may promote hair growth via induction of proteins in hair follicles, when used in combination with minoxidil. Contact your doctor before applying it. Does EZANIC 20% GEL cause redness of skin? Yes. EZANIC 20% GEL may cause burning, itching or redness of the skin (erythema) at the application site. Contact your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen. Is EZANIC 20% GEL safe in pregnancy? Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or are planning to have a baby before applying this medicine. Your doctor will decide whether you can use EZANIC 20% GEL. Can I apply face creams while using EZANIC 20% GEL? Yes, you may apply cosmetics after the EZANIC 20% GEL has dried. Do not wrap or bandage the skin unless your doctor has instructed to do so. Talk to your doctor for advice before using this medicine. References 1. Linda Skidmore-Roth. Azelaic acid. name: SALICARE 12% Ointment 30gm
description: Introduction About SALICARE 12% OINTMENT SALICARE 12% OINTMENT contains Salicylic acid which belongs to the group of medicines called Keratolytic agents. SALICARE 12% OINTMENT is used manage skin conditions such as psoriasis, dry, scaly skin conditions and acne. It is also used to manage dandruff, corn and calluses (thickened layers of skin) in affected individuals. SALICARE 12% OINTMENT is not recommended for use in patients allergic to Salicylic acid. It is also not recommended for use in patients with active inflammation/dermatitis, infection (at the application site), acute viral infection, skin malignancy, and/or tanned skin. Before applying SALICARE 12% OINTMENT, inform your doctor if you are scheduled for surgery, and/or suffering from any kidney problems. SALICARE 12% OINTMENT is generally not recommended for use in pregnant women. If you are a breastfeeding women, consult your doctor before using the medicine. Avoid applying the medicine on skin areas which might come in direct contact with infant’s skin. SALICARE 12% OINTMENT should be used with caution in children and adolescents (aged 1-15 years). It is also advised to be used with caution in elderly patients (aged above 65 years). Consult your doctor before applying the medicine. The most common side effects of applying SALICARE 12% OINTMENT are erythema (skin redness) or skin dryness. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsens. Uses Of SALICARE 12% OINTMENT It is used to manage: Psoriasis, dry, scaly skin conditions and acne Dandruff, corn & calluses (thickened layers of skin) in affected individuals How SALICARE 12% OINTMENT Works SALICARE 12% OINTMENT works by penetrating the affected area of skin and causing destruction to the bacteria which also reduces oil production in the skin thus managing the occurrence of skin conditions such as acne, blemishes, dandruff, and corn, calluses in affected individuals. How to use SALICARE 12% OINTMENT Apply SALICARE 12% OINTMENT as directed by your physician. It is for external use only. Wash your hands before use and work into a lather by adding water. Apply a thin layer and massage over wet skin or affected skin area. Avoid applying this medicine around your eyes, including eyelids. Side Effects Of SALICARE 12% OINTMENT Common Erythema (skin redness) Dryness of skin Rare Undesirable pigment loss at the site of application Scar Stop applying SALICARE 12% OINTMENT and contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following side effects: Excessive burning, stinging or peeling at the site of application How To Manage Side Effects Dry Skin Try moisturizing your skin with an ointment, cream, or lotion 2 or 3 times a day, or as often as needed. Moisturizers help to keep the area moisture, so they work best on damp skin. After you bathe, pat your skin dry then apply your moisturizer. Try to avoid using skin care products and soaps that contain alcohol, fragrances, dyes, or other chemicals. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy CONTRAINDICATED SALICARE 12% OINTMENT is not recommended for use in pregnant women. Consult your doctor before applying SALICARE 12% OINTMENT. Breastfeeding CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR If you are a breastfeeding women, consult your doctor before using SALICARE 12% OINTMENT. Avoid applying the medicine on skin areas which might come in direct contact with infant’s skin. Consult your doctor before applying the medicine. Kidney USE WITH CAUTION SALICARE 12% OINTMENT is used with caution in patients with kidney problems. Consult your doctor before applying the medicine. Allergy CONTRAINDICATED Do not use SALICARE 12% OINTMENT if you are allergic to Salicylic acid and/or any other ingredients of this medicine. Use In Pediatrics USE WITH CAUTION SALICARE 12% OINTMENT should be used with caution in children and adolescents (aged 1-15 years). Consult your doctor before applying the medicine. Use In Geriatrics USE WITH CAUTION SALICARE 12% OINTMENT should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged above 65 years). Consult your doctor before applying the medicine. Others SALICARE 12% OINTMENT is not recommended for use if you have : Active inflammation/dermatitis Infection at the application site Acute viral infection Skin malignancy Tanned skin Before applying SALICARE 12% OINTMENT, inform your doctor if you: Are scheduled for surgery Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Inform your doctor about your current list of medications, over the counter products such as vitamins, herbal supplements. Overdosage: If you or anyone else applied too much of SALICARE 12% OINTMENT or accidentally swallowed the medicine, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital to manage the overdose symptoms. A: SALICARE 12% OINTMENT is used to manage psoriasis, dry, scaly skin conditions, acne, dandruff, corn & calluses (thickened layers of skin) in affected individuals. Q: How to apply SALICARE 12% OINTMENT? A: Always apply SALICARE 12% OINTMENT as directed by your physician. It is for external use only. A: The most common side effects of using SALICARE 12% OINTMENT are erythema (skin redness), and/or dryness of skin. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsens. Q: How SALICARE 12% OINTMENT works? A: SALICARE 12% OINTMENT works by penetrating the affected area of skin and causing destruction to the bacteria which also reduces oil production in the skin thus managing and managing the occurrence of skin conditions such as acne, blemishes, dandruff, and corn & calluses in affected individuals. description: Introduction About PERSOL PLUS GEL PERSOL PLUS GEL is a combination of Adapalene and Benzoyl peroxide which belongs to the group of medicines called Antiacne agents. It is used in the management of acne. Acne vulgaris (commonly known as acne) is an inflammatory skin condition that occurs when the hair follicles present in the skin are clogged with excess oil and/or dead skin cells. It can also be aggravated by few bacteria (such as Propionibacterium acnes) and is highly common among on the teenagers and the young adults. It primarily affects the face, upper arms, trunk or back and is often characterized by pus-filled pimples, red bumps with inflammatory and non-inflammatory lesions. PERSOL PLUS GEL is suitable for use both in adults and in children (aged 9 years or older). Apply a thin layer of PERSOL PLUS GEL on the affected skin areas. Avoid contact of this medicine with your eyes, mouth, ears, nose or with open wounds. You must also protect your skin against sun light and against other light sources (such as UV lamps). Do not use PERSOL PLUS GEL if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. PERSOL PLUS GEL can be used in breastfeeding women if required. The most common side effects of using PERSOL PLUS GEL are dry skin, mild burning sensation and skin irritation, redness or scaling. Consult your doctor if they trouble you. Uses Of PERSOL PLUS GEL It is used in adults, children and in adolescents (aged 9 years or older) to: Manage acne How PERSOL PLUS GEL Works PERSOL PLUS GEL is a combination of two medicines namely, adapalene and benzoyl peroxide. Adapalene is a topical retinoid (a type of vitamin A). It modulates the skin cell cycle and manages the accumulation of excess sebum (natural oil produced by the skin) and dead skin cells on the hair follicles of the skin. It also reduces inflammation on the skin. Benzoyl peroxide is a keratolytic agent with antimicrobial properties. It improves skin’s tendency to exfoliate the dead skin cells naturally. It also reduces the number of acne-causing bacteria on the skin which can reduce the further spread of acne. Collectively, they unclog the hair follicles of the skin and exfoliates dead skin cells which reduces acne breakouts. How to use PERSOL PLUS GEL Apply a thin layer of this medicine on the affected skin areas or as directed by the physician. It is for topical use only. Wash your hands before and after application. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and health condition. Avoid contact of PERSOL PLUS GEL with your eyes, mouth, ears, nose, hair or with open wounds (cuts, scrapes or sunburn). Side Effects Of PERSOL PLUS GEL Common Dry skin Skin redness and scaling Burning sensation of the skin Skin irritation Uncommon Itching of the skin (pruritus) Sunburn Rare Stop using PERSOL PLUS GEL and consult your doctor immediately if you experience: Signs of allergic reaction (such as severe skin rash with itching of body parts, swelling of the eyes, face, lips or tongue causing throat tightness and breathing difficulties and feel faint) How To Manage Side Effects Skin redness and irritation: Place an icepack on the affected skin areas to ease the irritation. Avoid using harsh chemicals or soaps on the affected areas. Wear protective loose-fitting clothes while going outdoors. Regularly moisturize your skin. Avoid exposing your skin towards direct sunlight. If the condition did not improve, contact your doctor. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy PERSOL PLUS GEL is not recommended for use in pregnant women. Therefore, inform your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. If you became pregnant while using this medicine, stop using it and contact your doctor immediately. Breastfeeding PERSOL PLUS GEL can be used in breastfeeding women. However, do not apply this medicine on your chest to avoid exposing this medicine to the nursing infant. Allergy Talk to your doctor if you are allergic to Adapalene or Benzoyl peroxide. Others PERSOL PLUS GEL is not recommended for use if you: Have any cuts, scrapes, sunburn or eczema at the site of application Use in Pediatrics: PERSOL PLUS GEL can be used in children and adolescents (aged 9 years or older) if advised by the physician. Therefore, consult your doctor before using it. Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Before using PERSOL PLUS GEL, inform your doctor if you are using any of the following: Other anti-acne medicines (such as clindamycin) Skin cosmetics (such as hair perming solutions, astringents, toners, shaving lotion, abrasive soaps or cleansers) Overdosage: If you or anyone else applied excessive amount of PERSOL PLUS GEL, rinse your skin with plenty of cold water. If irritation persists, consult your doctor. No. Do not overuse this medicine. If you use more, you will not get rid of acne quicker. Instead, it may make your skin more irritated and red. Therefore, only apply the quantity mentioned by your doctor. What are the side effects of using PERSOL PLUS GEL? PERSOL PLUS GEL is generally safe with limited or no side effects. However, you may experience skin dryness, redness or irritation after applying this medicine. Contact your doctor if it troubles you. What is the use of PERSOL PLUS GEL? PERSOL PLUS GEL is used in the management of acne. How PERSOL PLUS GEL works? PERSOL PLUS GEL manages the accumulation of excess sebum (natural oil produced by the skin) and dead skin cells on the hair follicles of the skin. It also reduces inflammation on the skin and improves skin’s tendency to exfoliate the dead skin cells naturally. It also reduces the number of acne-causing bacteria on the skin which can reduce the further spread of acne. How to use PERSOL PLUS GEL? PERSOL PLUS GEL is for external use only. Take the required quantity of the medicine and apply on the affected skin areas. Avoid contact of this medicine with your eyes, ears, nose or any other mucous membranes. How long does it take for PERSOL PLUS GEL to work? It may take up to 2-3 weeks for PERSOL PLUS GEL to show improvement in your skin condition. However, this period may vary from person-to-person depending upon the skin condition. How long should I use PERSOL PLUS GEL? Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and health condition. You need to use PERSOL PLUS GEL for the stipulated duration prescribed by your doctor. Failing to do so may not result in adequate response. What to do if I forgot to apply PERSOL PLUS GEL? If you forgot to apply PERSOL PLUS GEL, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is time for the next application, skip the missed one and apply the next dose. Do not excessively apply PERSOL PLUS GEL to compensate the missed doses. Is PERSOL PLUS GEL safe? PERSOL PLUS GEL is safe at doses prescribed by the physician. Therefore, do not alter the dose of PERSOL PLUS GEL without consulting your doctor. Can I stop using PERSOL PLUS GEL without consulting your doctor? No. You should not stop using PERSOL PLUS GEL without consulting your doctor as it may reduce its effectiveness. Therefore, apply PERSOL PLUS GEL for the stipulated duration recommended by your doctor to achieve maximum results. Can PERSOL PLUS GEL be used in pregnant women? PERSOL PLUS GEL is not recommended for use in pregnant women. Therefore, inform your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. If you became pregnant while using this medicine, stop using it and contact your doctor immediately. References 1. KD. Tripathi. Drugs Acting on Skin and Mucous Membranes. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and health condition. You need to use ACNOVATE TRIO GEL for the stipulated duration prescribed by your doctor. Failing to do so may not result in adequate response. What to do if I forgot to apply ACNOVATE TRIO GEL? The safety and effectiveness of CLINBID 1.0% GEL in children under the age of 12 has not been established. name: Exazel 15% Cream 15gm
description: Introduction About EXAZEL 15% CREAM EXAZEL 15% CREAM contains Azelaic acid which belongs to the group of medicines called Dicarboxylic acids. It is used to manage common acne (acne vulgaris). It is also used for the management of mild to moderate papulopustular rosacea. Acne is a skin condition that occurs when the hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells. It causes whiteheads, blackheads or pimples. Rosacea is a skin condition that causes blushing or redness, pus-filled bumps and small visible blood vessels in the face. EXAZEL 15% CREAM should be applied with caution in patients with lung problems such as asthma. Consult your doctor before applying it. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before applying this medicine. Your doctor will decide whether you can use this medicine. EXAZEL 15% CREAM is generally not recommended for use in children under 12 years of age for the management of acne and also not recommended for use in children under 18 years of age for the management of rosacea. Consult your doctor before applying it. The most common side effects of applying EXAZEL 15% CREAM are burning, itching or redness of the skin (erythema) at the application site, scaling, pain, dryness, skin discolouration or irritation at the application site. Contact your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen. Uses Of EXAZEL 15% CREAM Common acne (acne vulgaris) Mild to moderate papulopustular rosacea How EXAZEL 15% CREAM Works EXAZEL 15% CREAM attacks the bacteria called propionibacterium acnes, which plays an essential part in causing acne. It also reduces growth of the harder outermost skin cells (keratin surface cells) that block the pores of the skin to cause blackheads and whiteheads. How to use EXAZEL 15% CREAM Apply EXAZEL 15% CREAM as directed by your physician. It is for external use only. Wash your hands with soap and water before and after using EXAZEL 15% CREAM. Apply a thin layer of this medicine on the affected area and rub it gently into the skin. Avoid applying this medicine around your eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes or open wounds. If it does, wash the eyes, mouth or other mucous membranes immediately with large amounts of cool water. Side Effects Of EXAZEL 15% CREAM Common Burning, itching or redness of the skin (erythema) at the application site Scaling, pain, dryness, skin discolouration or irritation at the application site Uncommon Greasy skin Acne or loss of skin colour Tingling Dermatitis Discomfort or swelling at the application site Rare Cracking of the lips, small blisters Eczema, ulceration Warmth at the site of application Allergic reaction such as urticaria or hives, rash at the site of application Worsening of asthma Stop applying EXAZEL 15% CREAM and contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following side effects: Allergic reaction such as rash, angioedema (swelling under the skin), swelling of face, eyes and dyspnoea (shortness of breath) How To Manage Side Effects Skin rash: Avoid hot bath because hot water can irritate your skin further. Do not scratch the affected area. Use sunscreen and wear protective clothing while going outside. Use unscented moisturizers to soothe and hydrate the affected area. Contact your doctor if the rashes worsen. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or are planning to have a baby before applying this medicine. Your doctor will decide whether you can use EXAZEL 15% CREAM. Breastfeeding EXAZEL 15% CREAM should be used with caution in breastfeeding women. Consult your doctor before applying it. Infants must not come into contact with managed skin or breasts. Driving and Using Machines EXAZEL 15% CREAM has no influence on the ability to drive and use machines. Allergy Do not apply EXAZEL 15% CREAM if you are allergic to Azelaic acid or any of the other ingredients of this medicine. Lungs EXAZEL 15% CREAM should be applied with caution in patients with lung problems such as asthma. Consult your doctor before applying it. Others Use in pediatrics: EXAZEL 15% CREAM is generally not recommended for use in children under 12 years of age for the management of acne. It is also not recommended for use in children under 18 years of age for the management of rosacea due to a lack of data on safety and efficacy. Consult your doctor before applying it. Use in geriatrics: There is limited information available on the use of EXAZEL 15% CREAM in elderly patients. Consult your doctor before applying it. Interactions A. Drug - Drug interactions: Tell your doctor if you are taking or have recently taken any other medicines, including medicines obtained without a prescription, vitamin supplement or herbal products. Overdosage: If you or anyone else accidentally used too much of EXAZEL 15% CREAM or if you or a child accidentally swallow the medicine, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Synopsis Drug : Azelaic acid Pharmacological Category : Dicarboxylic acids Therapeutic Indication : Common acne, Papulopustular rosacea Dosage Forms : Cream, Gel, Gel (Topical) More Information Keep EXAZEL 15% CREAM out of the sight and reach of children Store EXAZEL 15% CREAM below 30°C FAQs About EXAZEL 15% CREAM How long can I use EXAZEL 15% CREAM? How long EXAZEL 15% CREAM has to be used varies from person to person. It depends upon how bad your acne is when you start management. In general, you may notice a distinct improvement after 4 weeks. In case of no improvement after 1 month or if the acne or rosacea becomes worse, you should discontinue EXAZEL 15% CREAM and consult your doctor. How long does it take EXAZEL 15% CREAM to lighten skin? EXAZEL 15% CREAM when applied twice daily for several (up to 8 months), skin lightening starts after 1 to 2 months of using it. But when EXAZEL 15% CREAM is used in combination with a medicine called tretinoin causes more skin lightening after 3 months than EXAZEL 15% CREAM alone. Consult your doctor for advice. Can I use EXAZEL 15% CREAM for hair growth? Yes. EXAZEL 15% CREAM may promote hair growth via induction of proteins in hair follicles, when used in combination with minoxidil. Contact your doctor before applying it. Does EXAZEL 15% CREAM cause redness of skin? Yes. EXAZEL 15% CREAM may cause burning, itching or redness of the skin (erythema) at the application site. Contact your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen. Is EXAZEL 15% CREAM safe in pregnancy? Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or are planning to have a baby before applying this medicine. Your doctor will decide whether you can use EXAZEL 15% CREAM. Can I apply face creams while using EXAZEL 15% CREAM? Yes, you may apply cosmetics after the EXAZEL 15% CREAM has dried. Do not wrap or bandage the skin unless your doctor has instructed to do so. Talk to your doctor for advice before using this medicine. References 1. Linda Skidmore-Roth. Azelaic acid.
