Consult your doctor before using BENZRIN AC 2.5% GEL(TOPICAL). Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Before applying BENZRIN AC 2.5% GEL(TOPICAL), inform your doctor if you are taking or using any of the following medicine: Medicines used to manage various skin diseases (Ex. dapsone) Topical hydroquinone (medicine used to remove dark patches of the skin) Isotretinoin, topical tretinoin (used to manage acne) Topical anaesthetics (used to relieve pain and itching) Ex. benzocaine, lignocaine B. Drug-Food interactions: Before applying BENZRIN AC 2.5% GEL(TOPICAL) inform your doctor if you are having any allergies to any other medicines, foods, preservatives or dyes. Overdosage: If you or anyone else accidentally applies more of BENZRIN AC 2.5% GEL(TOPICAL) or accidently ingested BENZRIN AC 2.5% GEL(TOPICAL), consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Symptoms of overuse of this medicine is severe skin irritation. It is also used to manage dandruff, corn and calluses (thickened layers of skin) in affected individuals. DERSOL 12% OINTMENT is not recommended for use in patients allergic to Salicylic acid. It is also not recommended for use in patients with active inflammation/dermatitis, infection (at the application site), acute viral infection, skin malignancy, and/or tanned skin. Before applying DERSOL 12% OINTMENT, inform your doctor if you are scheduled for surgery, and/or suffering from any kidney problems. DERSOL 12% OINTMENT is generally not recommended for use in pregnant women. If you are a breastfeeding women, consult your doctor before using the medicine. Avoid applying the medicine on skin areas which might come in direct contact with infant’s skin. DERSOL 12% OINTMENT should be used with caution in children and adolescents (aged 1-15 years). It is also advised to be used with caution in elderly patients (aged above 65 years). Consult your doctor before applying the medicine. The most common side effects of applying DERSOL 12% OINTMENT are erythema (skin redness) or skin dryness. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsens. name: ISOLOX 10 Tablet 10's
description: Introduction About ISOLOX 10 TABLET ISOLOX 10 TABLET contains Isotretinoin, a retinoid medication specifically designed to manage severe acne in adults and children over 12 years of age. It is particularly effective for nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring when other anti-acne treatments have failed. Acne is a skin condition characterized by inflammatory spots, oily skin, and painful nodular lesions that commonly affect the face, chest, and back. Take ISOLOX 10 TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor, following the recommended dose and duration. It is best taken with food, preferably at the same time each day, to reduce the chances of missing a dose. It may take a few weeks before you notice an improvement in your symptoms but continue taking the medication as directed to achieve optimal results. If your condition does not improve after several weeks, consult your doctor for further advice. This medication can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, so limit sun exposure and use sunscreen when outdoors. It may also make your skin more fragile, so avoid waxing or laser treatments during therapy. Dryness of the lips, mouth, and eyes is another potential side effect—stay hydrated and use moisturizers or lubricating eye drops as needed Common side effects include dry skin, rashes, and elevated liver enzymes. While these are generally mild and tend to subside as your body adjusts to the medication, inform your doctor if they persist or cause discomfort. ISOLOX 10 TABLET is known to cause birth defects, so it should not be used during pregnancy or if you are planning to conceive. Always discuss your treatment plan with your doctor to ensure safety and effectiveness. Uses Of ISOLOX 10 TABLET Severe acne in adults and children (older than 12 years of age) Benefits of ISOLOX 10 TABLET for Acne: ISOLOX 10 TABLET is highly effective in managing severe acne conditions such as nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring. It works by reducing the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, unclogging pores, and decreasing inflammation, which helps to clear up existing acne and prevent new breakouts. This leads to smoother, healthier skin and reduces the risk of long-term scarring. Additionally, it targets the underlying causes of severe acne, making it a reliable choice for those who have not responded to other treatments. Always consult your doctor to ensure it is suitable for your condition. How ISOLOX 10 TABLET Works ISOLOX 10 TABLET work by targeting the root causes of severe acne. They reduce the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, which helps prevent pores from becoming clogged. This, in turn, reduces the growth of acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Isotretinoin also promotes the turnover of skin cells, preventing the formation of new acne lesions. Together, these actions help clear up existing acne and reduce the chances of scarring, making it an effective treatment for stubborn or severe acne conditions. How to use ISOLOX 10 TABLET Take ISOLOX 10 TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the capsule whole with a glass of water; do not crush or chew it. It is recommended to take the capsule with food to improve absorption and reduce stomach discomfort. Take it at the same time each day to maintain consistent levels of the medication in your body. Follow the prescribed dosage and duration carefully. Do not stop the medication abruptly without consulting your doctor, even if your symptoms improve. Regular follow-ups and blood tests may be required to monitor your progress and ensure safe usage. Avoid alcohol, excessive sun exposure, and waxing or laser treatments during the treatment period. Use sunscreen and moisturizers as recommended by your doctor. What if I Forget to take ISOLOX 10 TABLET: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose—do not double the dose to make up for it. Overdosage of ISOLOX 10 TABLET – In case you or anybody else accidently take too much of ISOLOX 10 TABLET, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Symptoms of ISOLOX 10 TABLET overdose are severe headache, abdominal pain, nausea, dizziness, redness of face, vomiting, somnolence, irritability, and itching. Side Effects Of ISOLOX 10 TABLET Like all medicines ISOLOX 10 TABLET may cause certain side effects, although not everyone gets them Common Side Effects of ISOLOX 10 TABLET: Dry skin More fragile and red skin than usual, especially of the face Back, muscle or joint pain (particularly in children and teenagers) Raised liver enzymes Changed blood fat and cholesterol levels Easy bruising, bleeding or clotting Headache Protein or blood in the urine Becoming more prone to get infections Sore or inflamed throat and nose Stop taking ISOLOX 10 TABLET and consult your doctor immediately in case you experience any of the following: Persistent pain in your lower back or buttocks (signs of sacroiliitis) Severe skin reactions (Ex. erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis) (blistering and peeling of skin, severe rashes, fever, multiple lesions especially in mouth, nose, eyes and genitals, conjunctivitis, flu-like symptoms) Feeling depressed with suicidal thoughts Serious reactions (trouble breathing or swallowing due to sudden swelling of the throat, face, lips and mouth, sudden swelling of the hands, feet and ankles, hives, bruises, eczema, bruising, red patches on hands and legs) Rhabdomyolysis (muscle weakness along with trouble moving arms or legs, painful, swollen, bruised areas of the body, dark urine, reduced or no urination, confusion or dehydration) Hepatitis (yellow skin or eyes, tiredness) Kidney inflammation (difficulty urinating, swollen and puffy eyelids, excessive tiredness) How To Manage Side Effects Dry Skin Hydrate Regularly: Drink plenty of water throughout the day to keep your skin hydrated from within. Aim for at least 8–10 glasses daily. Use a Gentle Cleanser: Opt for a mild, fragrance-free cleanser to avoid further irritation. Avoid harsh soaps or scrubs that can strip the skin of natural oils. Moisturize Frequently: Apply a rich, non-comedogenic moisturizer to your face and body at least twice a day, especially after washing. Look for products with hydrating ingredients like hyaluronic acid or ceramides. Protect Your Lips: Use a moisturizing lip balm, preferably one with SPF, to prevent and treat cracked lips caused by dryness. Reapply as needed throughout the day. Avoid Long, Hot Showers: Hot water can strip your skin of its natural moisture. Take shorter showers with lukewarm water to minimize dryness. Humidify Your Environment: Use a humidifier in your home to add moisture to the air, especially during winter or in dry climates. Apply Sunscreen: Use a broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher daily to protect your sensitive skin from sun damage and prevent further dryness. Limit Exfoliation: Avoid physical or chemical exfoliants, as isotretinoin makes your skin more delicate and prone to irritation. Choose Gentle Fabrics: Wear soft, breathable fabrics like cotton to reduce friction and irritation on your dry skin. Seek Medical Advice: If dryness becomes severe or persistent despite home remedies, consult your doctor for additional treatment options or product recommendations. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy CONTRAINDICATED Human and animal studies have shown that isotretinoin is teratogenic in nature. Birth defects such as abnormalities of the face, eyes, ears, skull, central nervous system, cardiovascular system, and thymus and parathyroid glands or IQ less than score of 85 have been reported in female patients who were pregnant or became pregnant while on therapy with isotretinoin. Therefore, ISOLOX 10 TABLET is considered unsafe for use during pregnancy. Women of childbearing potential must use a reliable contraceptive method to avoid becoming pregnant. If you accidentally became pregnant while taking this medicine, stop taking it and consult your gynaecologist for further evaluation. It is also not recommended for you to get pregnant for one month after stopping isotretinoin tablets because some medicine may still be left in your body. Consult your doctor before taking it. Breastfeeding CONTRAINDICATED It is not known whether this medicine is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects, nursing mothers should not receive ISOLOX 10 TABLET Driving and Using Machines USE WITH CAUTION Do not drive or operate machinery if you experience dizziness, drowsiness or decreased night vision after taking ISOLOX 10 TABLET. Alcohol CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR Avoid consuming alcohol while taking ISOLOX 10 TABLET as it may increase side effects. Inform your doctor if you have an habit of chronic alcoholism. Kidney USE WITH CAUTION ISOLOX 10 TABLET should be used with caution in patients with kidney problems. Consult your doctor before taking it. Liver CONTRAINDICATED ISOLOX 10 TABLET is not recommended for use in patients with liver disease. Consult your doctor before taking it. Allergy CONTRAINDICATED Do not take ISOLOX 10 TABLET if you are allergic to Isotretinoin, soya, peanuts or any of the other ingredients of this medicine. Lungs USE WITH CAUTION ISOLOX 10 TABLET should be used with caution in patients having asthma. Consult your doctor before taking it. Use In Pediatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR The use of isotretinoin tablets in pediatric patients less than 12 years of age has not been studied. The use of isotretinoin for severe recalcitrant nodular acne in adolescents ages 12 to 17 years under careful medical supervision. Extreme caution should be taken if the child is suffering from metabolic or structural bone disease. Use In Geriatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR There is no proper information about the use of ISOLOX 10 TABLET in elderly patients. Consult your doctor before taking it. Others ISOLOX 10 TABLET is not recommended for use if you have: High blood fat levels High levels of Vitamin A Before taking ISOLOX 10 TABLET inform your doctor if you: Have or had mental illness or family history of mental illness such as depression, mood disorders, psychosis, aggressive behaviour, or hurting or killing self Have diabetes Are fructose intolerant Are overweight Safety Advice Always take isotretinoin with a meal to improve its absorption. Drink plenty of water to prevent dryness in your mouth and throat. Isotretinoin is related to vitamin A, so extra supplementation can cause toxicity. Avoid Excessive Sun Exposure: Wear sunscreen and protective clothing as isotretinoin can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Moisturize Regularly: Use lip balms and non-comedogenic moisturizers to manage dryness of lips and skin. Use Effective Birth Control: Isotretinoin can cause severe birth defects. Therefore, women must use reliable contraception as isotretinoin can cause severe birth defects. Do Not Donate Blood: Avoid donating blood while on isotretinoin and for at least a month after stopping it, as it can harm pregnant recipients. Follow Regular Check-Ups: Attend scheduled visits with your doctor for blood tests and monitoring. Avoid Waxing or Laser Treatments: Your skin is fragile during treatment and prone to scarring. Alcohol can increase the risk of liver problems, so limit or avoid it. Notify your doctor about severe dryness, mood changes, or unusual symptoms. Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Before taking ISOLOX 10 TABLET, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines: Vitamin A supplements Medicines used to manage bacterial infections (Ex. minocycline, doxycycline) Phenytoin (used to manage fits) Medicines used to manage various inflammatory conditions (Ex. betamethasone, prednisolone, dexamethasone) Medicines used to manage pregnancy (Ex. Norethindrone, ethinyl Oestradiol) St. John’s wort (herbal medicine used to manage mental disorders) Other medicines used to manage acne like keratolytic or exfoliative agents (Ex. salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide) Synopsis Drug : Isotretinoin Pharmacological Category : Retinoids Therapeutic Indication : Severe acne Dosage Forms : Tablet, Soft gel Capsule, Capsule More Information Relevant Health Articles – Hormonal Acne: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment Anti-Acne Food: Eat Healthy To Heal Acne -Infographic FAQs About ISOLOX 10 TABLET Q: What is ISOLOX 10 TABLET used for? A: ISOLOX 10 TABLET is used to manage severe acne (nodular or cystic acne) that does not respond to other treatments like antibiotics. It works by reducing oil production in the skin and preventing clogged pores. Q: How should I take ISOLOX 10 TABLET? A: Take ISOLOX 10 TABLET as prescribed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily with food. Swallow the capsule whole with water, and avoid breaking or crushing it. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully for the best results. Q: What are the common side effects of ISOLOX 10 TABLET? A: Common side effects include dry skin, chapped lips, dry eyes, nosebleeds, and mild stomach discomfort. If you experience severe reactions like mood changes, persistent headaches, or vision problems, consult your doctor immediately. Q: Can ISOLOX 10 TABLET be taken during pregnancy? A: No, ISOLOX 10 TABLET should not be taken during pregnancy as it can cause severe birth defects. Women of childbearing age must use effective contraception during and at least one month after treatment. Q: Is ISOLOX 10 TABLET safe for long-term use? A: Isotretinoin is not usually prescribed for long-term use due to its potential side effects. Treatment duration is typically limited to 16–20 weeks. Always follow your doctor’s advice regarding treatment duration. Q: Can I use cosmetics while on ISOLOX 10 TABLET? A: Yes, you can use non-comedogenic and fragrance-free cosmetics. Avoid abrasive cleansers, harsh exfoliants, or acne products containing benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid, as these may irritate your skin. Q: Does ISOLOX 10 TABLET cause hair loss? A: Temporary hair thinning or hair loss can occur in some individuals during treatment. This side effect typically resolves after completing the course. If hair loss persists, consult your doctor. Q: Can I drink alcohol while taking ISOLOX 10 TABLET? A: It is advised to avoid alcohol while taking ISOLOX 10 TABLET, as it can increase the risk of liver damage and worsen side effects like dizziness or drowsiness. Q: How long does it take for ISOLOX 10 TABLET to work? A: You may start noticing improvements within 4–8 weeks, but the full effects are usually seen after completing the treatment course. Be patient and continue using the medicine as prescribed. Q: What precautions should I take while using ISOLOX 10 TABLET? A: Avoid excessive sun exposure and use sunscreen. Do not donate blood during and for one month after treatment. Inform your doctor about any other medications or supplements you are taking. Use a reliable birth control to avoid becoming pregnant while taking ISOLOX 10 TABLET. Do not undergo cosmetic procedures such as skin waxing, dermabrasion, laser, or artificial UV light detanning while taking ISOLOX 10 TABLET without consulting your doctor. Q: Can ISOLOX 10 TABLET be used by men? A: Yes, ISOLOX 10 TABLET is safe for men to use for severe acne. However, male patients planning to father a child need not take special precautions, as isotretinoin does not affect sperm. Can ISOLOX 10 TABLET cause irregular periods? According to some studies, menstrual irregularity was observed during management follow-ups. Consult your doctor if you experience irregularity in your periods during management with ISOLOX 10 TABLET. Is ISOLOX 10 TABLET safe to take in pregnancy? No. ISOLOX 10 TABLET is not recommended for use in pregnant women and women planning a pregnancy. Inform your doctor if you become pregnant during management with ISOLOX 10 TABLET. It is not recommended to get pregnant for one month after stopping ISOLOX 10 TABLET management because some medicine may still be left in your body. Consult your doctor before taking it. Contraception must be used for a month before taking ISOLOX 10 TABLET, during management and for a month afterwards. Discuss with your doctor regarding suitable contraceptive methods. Can I play sports during ISOLOX 10 TABLET management? Cut down on extreme exercise and physical activity as ISOLOX 10 TABLET can cause muscle and joint pain especially in children and teenagers taking up vigorous physical activity. Consult your doctor if you can play sports during this management. Can I go out in the sun during ISOLOX 10 TABLET management? Sensitivity to light may increase during management with ISOLOX 10 TABLET so, avoid going too much into the sun and don’t use a sun-lamp or sun-bed. Before you go out in the sun, wear sunglasses and use sunscreen with a high protection factor (SPF 15 or higher). Can undergo cosmetic procedures while taking ISOLOX 10 TABLET? No. Do not undergo cosmetic procedures such as skin waxing, dermabrasion, laser, or artificial UV light detanning while taking ISOLOX 10 TABLET or at least for 6 months after stopping it as they could cause scarring, skin irritation, or changes in your skin colour. Consult your doctor before undergoing any cosmetic procedure while taking ISOLOX 10 TABLET. References 1. KD Tripathi. Drugs Acting on Skin and Mucous Membranes. name: Clinxa Gel 20gm
description: Introduction About CLINXA GEL CLINXA GEL contains Clindamycin, which belongs to the group of medicines called Antibiotics. It is used in the management of acne vulgaris. Acne vulgaris is a common skin condition that occurs when hair follicles get blocked with oil and dead skin cells. Symptoms include whiteheads, blackheads, small red, tender bumps, pimples, and pus-filled lumps on the skin. Before applying CLINXA GEL, inform your doctor if you have or ever had diarrhea, bloody diarrhea and pseudomembranous colitis. CLINXA GEL is not recommended for use if you have a history of regional enteritis (inflammation of the small intestine), ulcerative colitis (inflammation of the large intestine) or antibiotic-associated colitis. CLINXA GEL should be used with caution during pregnancy or by breastfeeding women only if clearly needed. The safety and effectiveness of CLINXA GEL in children under the age of 12 has not been established. The most common side effects of applying CLINXA GEL are burning, itching, and redness of the skin. Consult your doctor if symptoms worsen. Uses Of CLINXA GEL Manage acne vulgaris How CLINXA GEL Works CLINXA GEL acts against the bacteria by binding to the 50S subunit of the bacterial ribosome (site of protein synthesis), which in turn manages protein synthesis and kills the infection-causing bacteria. How to use CLINXA GEL Apply CLINXA GEL as advised by your physician. It is for external use only. Wash your hands before use. Wash and dry the whole area, apply a thin film once daily to the skin where acne lesions appear and use enough to cover the entire affected area. In case of contact with the eyes, mouth or nostrils, rinse it off immediately and thoroughly with water. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration for you depending on your age, body weight and disease condition. (a sign of bowel inflammation, pseudomembranous colitis) Warning & Precautions Pregnancy The safety and effectiveness of CLINXA GEL in pregnant women or women planning to have a baby have not been established yet. It will be given to you by the doctor only if clearly needed. Consult your doctor before applying CLINXA GEL. Breastfeeding CLINXA GEL should be used with caution in breastfeeding women as it is not known if the medicine is excreted in human milk. Your doctor will decide whether to discontinue nursing or the medicine, considering the benefits to the mother and baby. If it is applied to the chest, care should be taken to avoid accidental ingestion by the infant. Consult your doctor before applying CLINXA GEL. Allergy Do not apply CLINXA GEL if you are allergic to Clindamycin or any other ingredients of this medicine. Others CLINXA GEL is not recommended for use if you: Have regional enteritis (inflammation of the small intestine) or ulcerative colitis (inflammation of the large intestine) Have a history of antibiotic-associated colitis Before applying CLINXA GEL inform your doctor if you: Diarrhea, bloody diarrhea Pseudomembranous colitis (inflammation of colon) Atopic individuals (more prone to allergies) Use in pediatrics: Safety and effectiveness of CLINXA GEL in children under the age of 12 have not been established. Consult your doctor before applying CLINXA GEL. Interactions A. name: Dremz Cream 20gm
description: Introduction About DREMZ CREAM DREMZ CREAM is a combination of Hydroquinone, Tretinoin, Mometasone furoate which belongs to the group of medicines called Depigmenting agents, Retinoids and Corticosteroids respectively. It is used in adults for the management of moderate to severe melasma (dark spots on the skin) in association with sun-avoidance measures, like using sunscreens and wearing protective clothing. Melasma is one of the most frequently acquired hyperpigmentation (excess melanin production) disorders with symptoms such as symmetrical brown patches on sun exposed areas mainly on face. It is advised to avoid exposure to sun during management with DREMZ CREAM for better results. While going out apply sunscreens and wear full covering protective clothes. Before using DREMZ CREAM inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney, lung or heart diseases. Safety and efficacy of DREMZ CREAM is not established in pregnant women and in children below 12 years of age. Ask for your doctor’s advice before using. DREMZ CREAM should be used with caution in breastfeeding women. The most common side effects of using DREMZ CREAM are mild burning, stinging, redness and dryness. Consult your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen or doesn’t improve. Uses Of DREMZ CREAM It is used in adults to Manages moderate to severe melasma (dark spots on the skin) How DREMZ CREAM Works DREMZ CREAM helps in managing melasma where Hydroquinone is a skin bleaching agent that blocks enzyme tyrosinase which is responsible for the production of melanin that cause pigmentation. Thus, it helps for fading of dark spots in skin. Tretinoin helps to recover the damage to the skin caused by sun exposure (photodamage) by thickening skin layer and loss of keratinized cells.it helps to rejuvenate the skin. Mometasone furoate blocks prostaglandin synthesis and reduces redness, swelling and itching caused by tretinoin and other skin infections. How to use DREMZ CREAM Apply DREMZ CREAM as advised by your physician. It is for external use only. Wash your hands before and after applying DREMZ CREAM. Wash your face with a mild soap and dry properly. Apply DREMZ CREAM at night and gently massage it in until it is absorbed. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, mouth, mucous membrane. Avoid exposure to sunlight while using this medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition. Side Effects Of DREMZ CREAM Common Mild burning Stinging Redness Dryness Stop using DREMZ CREAM and consult your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following: Infraorbital and paranasal fissures How To Manage Side Effects Application Site Reactions Apply cool compress or wet cloth over affected area. Avoid hot bath because hot water can irritate your skin further. Do not scratch the affected area. Use protective clothing when going outdoors. Regularly moisturize your skin and apply calamine lotion as a coolant. Contact doctor if it is not subsiding. Dry Skin Drink plenty of water, milk, honey and stay hydrated. Apply sunflower oil, coconut oil ,aloe vera or petroleum jelly to moisturize skin. Contact doctor if it doesn’t improve. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR The safety and efficacy of DREMZ CREAM is not being established in pregnant women. Consult with your doctor before using. Breastfeeding USE WITH CAUTION DREMZ CREAM should be used with caution in breast feeding women. Consult with your doctor before using. Allergy CONTRAINDICATED Do not use DREMZ CREAM if you are allergic to Hydroquinone, Tretinoin, Mometasone or any other constituents of this medicine. Consult your doctor before using. Use In Pediatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR The safety and efficacy of DREMZ CREAM is not being established in children below 12 years of age. Consult with your child’s doctor before using it for your child. Use In Geriatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR There is no information on the use of DREMZ CREAM in elderly patients. Consult your doctor before using DREMZ CREAM. Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Before using DREMZ CREAM, inform your doctor if you are taking, have taken or might take any other medicine, including prescription, non-prescription or any herbal medicine. Overdosage: If you or anyone else accidentally ingests or apply too much of DREMZ CREAM, consult your doctor immediately. Synopsis Drug : Hydroquinone, Tretinoin, Mometasone Pharmacological Category : Hypopigmenting agents, Retinoids, Corticosteroids Therapeutic Indication : Melasma Dosage Forms : Cream, Gel, Ointment, Soap More Information Storage Keep DREMZ CREAM out of reach of children Store DREMZ CREAM at room temperature not exceeding 25°C FAQs About DREMZ CREAM Q: What is DREMZ CREAM used for? A: DREMZ CREAM is used in adults for the management of moderate to severe melasma (dark spots on the skin) in association with sun-avoidance measures, like using sunscreens and wearing protective clothing. Consult doctor before using. Q: How to use DREMZ CREAM? A: Apply DREMZ CREAM as advised by your physician. It is for external use only. Wash your hands before and after applying DREMZ CREAM. Wash your face with a mild soap and dry properly and gently massage the medicine until it is absorbed. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, mouth, mucous membrane. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition. Q: Can I use DREMZ CREAM to manage wounds? A: DREMZ CREAM is not recommended to use on wounds and ulcerated skin . Consult doctor before using DREMZ CREAM. Q: Do I need to take any precaution while using DREMZ CREAM? A: It is advised to reduce exposure to sun during management with DREMZ CREAM for better results. While going out apply sunscreens and wear full covering protective clothes. Exposure to sunlight or ultra-violet light will cause repigmentation of lightened skin. Do not apply DREMZ CREAM to broken skin. Q: What is the best time to use DREMZ CREAM? A: It is advised to use DREMZ CREAM before bedtime. This will reduce the chances of exposure of the managed skin to sun. However, ask for your doctor’s advice before using. References 1. KD Tripathi. name: DERIVA I 20 Capsule 10's
description: Introduction About DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE contains Isotretinoin, a retinoid medication specifically designed to manage severe acne in adults and children over 12 years of age. It is particularly effective for nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring when other anti-acne treatments have failed. Acne is a skin condition characterized by inflammatory spots, oily skin, and painful nodular lesions that commonly affect the face, chest, and back. Take DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE exactly as prescribed by your doctor, following the recommended dose and duration. It is best taken with food, preferably at the same time each day, to reduce the chances of missing a dose. It may take a few weeks before you notice an improvement in your symptoms but continue taking the medication as directed to achieve optimal results. If your condition does not improve after several weeks, consult your doctor for further advice. This medication can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, so limit sun exposure and use sunscreen when outdoors. It may also make your skin more fragile, so avoid waxing or laser treatments during therapy. Dryness of the lips, mouth, and eyes is another potential side effect—stay hydrated and use moisturizers or lubricating eye drops as needed Common side effects include dry skin, rashes, and elevated liver enzymes. While these are generally mild and tend to subside as your body adjusts to the medication, inform your doctor if they persist or cause discomfort. DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE is known to cause birth defects, so it should not be used during pregnancy or if you are planning to conceive. Always discuss your treatment plan with your doctor to ensure safety and effectiveness. Uses Of DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE Severe acne in adults and children (older than 12 years of age) Benefits of DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE for Acne: DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE is highly effective in managing severe acne conditions such as nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring. It works by reducing the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, unclogging pores, and decreasing inflammation, which helps to clear up existing acne and prevent new breakouts. This leads to smoother, healthier skin and reduces the risk of long-term scarring. Additionally, it targets the underlying causes of severe acne, making it a reliable choice for those who have not responded to other treatments. Always consult your doctor to ensure it is suitable for your condition. How DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE Works DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE work by targeting the root causes of severe acne. They reduce the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, which helps prevent pores from becoming clogged. This, in turn, reduces the growth of acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Isotretinoin also promotes the turnover of skin cells, preventing the formation of new acne lesions. Together, these actions help clear up existing acne and reduce the chances of scarring, making it an effective treatment for stubborn or severe acne conditions. How to use DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE Take DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the capsule whole with a glass of water; do not crush or chew it. It is recommended to take the capsule with food to improve absorption and reduce stomach discomfort. Take it at the same time each day to maintain consistent levels of the medication in your body. Follow the prescribed dosage and duration carefully. Do not stop the medication abruptly without consulting your doctor, even if your symptoms improve. Regular follow-ups and blood tests may be required to monitor your progress and ensure safe usage. Avoid alcohol, excessive sun exposure, and waxing or laser treatments during the treatment period. Use sunscreen and moisturizers as recommended by your doctor. What if I Forget to take DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose—do not double the dose to make up for it. Overdosage of DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE – In case you or anybody else accidently take too much of DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Symptoms of DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE overdose are severe headache, abdominal pain, nausea, dizziness, redness of face, vomiting, somnolence, irritability, and itching. Side Effects Of DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE Like all medicines DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE may cause certain side effects, although not everyone gets them Common Side Effects of DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE: Dry skin More fragile and red skin than usual, especially of the face Back, muscle or joint pain (particularly in children and teenagers) Raised liver enzymes Changed blood fat and cholesterol levels Easy bruising, bleeding or clotting Headache Protein or blood in the urine Becoming more prone to get infections Sore or inflamed throat and nose Stop taking DERIVA I 20 CAPSULE and consult your doctor immediately in case you experience any of the following: Persistent pain in your lower back or buttocks (signs of sacroiliitis) Severe skin reactions (Ex. erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis) (blistering and peeling of skin, severe rashes, fever, multiple lesions especially in mouth, nose, eyes and genitals, conjunctivitis, flu-like symptoms) Feeling depressed with suicidal thoughts Serious reactions (trouble breathing or swallowing due to sudden swelling of the throat, face, lips and mouth, sudden swelling of the hands, feet and ankles, hives, bruises, eczema, bruising, red patches on hands and legs) Rhabdomyolysis (muscle weakness along with trouble moving arms or legs, painful, swollen, bruised areas of the body, dark urine, reduced or no urination, confusion or dehydration) Hepatitis (yellow skin or eyes, tiredness) Kidney inflammation (difficulty urinating, swollen and puffy eyelids, excessive tiredness) How To Manage Side Effects Dry Skin Hydrate Regularly: Drink plenty of water throughout the day to keep your skin hydrated from within. Aim for at least 8–10 glasses daily. Use a Gentle Cleanser: Opt for a mild, fragrance-free cleanser to avoid further irritation. Avoid harsh soaps or scrubs that can strip the skin of natural oils. Moisturize Frequently: Apply a rich, non-comedogenic moisturizer to your face and body at least twice a day, especially after washing. description: Introduction About CLINDAFIN N GEL CLINDAFIN N GEL is a combination of Clindamycin and Nicotinamide which belongs to a group of medicines called Lincomycin antibiotics and Vitamin B3 complex, respectively. CLINDAFIN N GEL is used to manage mild to moderate acne which is a skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells which may occur due to variety of causes such as genetics, fluctuating hormone levels, stress, high humidity or using oily or greasy personal care products which may affect people of all ages. It is characterized by symptoms such as open or closed plugged pores, small red & tender bumps, pimples, large, solid or painful lumps under the skin and painful & pus-filled lumps under the skin. Before using CLINDAFIN N GEL inform your doctor if you have liver, kidney, lung or heart diseases. Avoid applying CLINDAFIN N GEL to a cut, scrapped, sunburnt or eczema affected skin. CLINDAFIN N GEL should be used with caution in pregnant and in breastfeeding women. CLINDAFIN N GEL is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (below 12 years). Consult your doctor before applying. The most common side effects of using CLINDAFIN N GEL are skin inflammation, contact dermatitis (red, itchy rash), inflammation of hair follicles, itchy skin, dry skin and peeling of skin. Consult your doctor if any of these symptoms worsen. Uses Of CLINDAFIN N GEL Manage mild to moderate acne How CLINDAFIN N GEL Works CLINDAFIN N GEL helps to manage acne, where Clindamycin reduces free fatty acid concentrations on the skin and suppresses the growth of Propionibacterium acnes (Corynebacterium acnes), a bacteria found in sebaceous glands and follicles and Nicotinamide exerts anti-inflammatory effect in acne and interrupts sebum production. How to use CLINDAFIN N GEL Apply CLINDAFIN N GEL as advised by your physician. It is for external use only. Before applying the medicine normally wash and dry the affected area and apply a thin layer of this medicine on the affected area. Managed areas on the face need not be covered with a plaster or bandage. Do not apply this medicine beyond the recommended duration. Avoid applying CLINDAFIN N GEL around your eyes, including eyelids. Rinse it off with water if you accidentally get it in these areas. Side Effects Of CLINDAFIN N GEL Common Contact dermatitis (red, itchy rash) Inflammation of hair follicles Itchy skin Dry skin Peeling of skin How To Manage Side Effects Skin rash/Itchy skin: Avoid hot bath because hot water can irritate your skin further. Do not scratch the affected area. Use protective clothing when going outdoors. Regularly moisturize your skin and apply calamine lotion as a coolant. Discuss with your doctor if the symptom worsens. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy CLINDAFIN N GEL should be used with caution in pregnant women. Consult your doctor before applying. Breastfeeding CLINDAFIN N GEL should be used with caution in breastfeeding women. Consult your doctor before applying. Allergy CLINDAFIN N GEL is not recommended for use if you are allergic to Clindamycin, Nicotinamide or any other ingredients of this medicine. Others CLINDAFIN N GEL is not recommended for use if you have: Eczema (skin inflammation) Cut, scrapped, sunburnt skin Use in Pediatrics: CLINDAFIN N GEL is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (below 12 years). Consult your doctor before using it for your child. Use in Geriatrics: There is no information on the use of CLINDAFIN N GEL in elderly patients. Consult with your doctor before using. Interactions A. Drug - Drug interactions: Before using CLINDAFIN N GEL, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines: Acepromazine (used a sedative/tranquilizer) Acetaminophen (used to manage pain and inflammation) Overdosage: If you or anyone else accidentally ingests or applies too much of CLINDAFIN N GEL, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Managed areas on the face need not be covered with a plaster or bandage. Do not apply this medicine on your face beyond 5 days. Avoid applying CLINDAFIN N GEL around your eyes, including eyelids. Is CLINDAFIN N GEL safe to use in pregnant and breastfeeding women? CLINDAFIN N GEL should be used with caution during pregnancy, women planning for pregnancy and in breastfeeding women. Consult your doctor before applying. Can CLINDAFIN N GEL cause skin irritation or itchy skin? CLINDAFIN N GEL may cause skin irritation or itchy skin. Avoid hot bath because hot water can irritate your skin further. Do not scratch the affected area. Use protective clothing when going outdoors. description: Introduction About CLINVIVA GEL CLINVIVA GEL contains Clindamycin, which belongs to the group of medicines called Antibiotics. It is used in the management of acne vulgaris. Acne vulgaris is a common skin condition that occurs when hair follicles get blocked with oil and dead skin cells. Symptoms include whiteheads, blackheads, small red, tender bumps, pimples, and pus-filled lumps on the skin. Before applying CLINVIVA GEL, inform your doctor if you have or ever had diarrhea, bloody diarrhea and pseudomembranous colitis. CLINVIVA GEL is not recommended for use if you have a history of regional enteritis (inflammation of the small intestine), ulcerative colitis (inflammation of the large intestine) or antibiotic-associated colitis. CLINVIVA GEL should be used with caution during pregnancy or by breastfeeding women only if clearly needed. The safety and effectiveness of CLINVIVA GEL in children under the age of 12 has not been established. The most common side effects of applying CLINVIVA GEL are burning, itching, and redness of the skin. Consult your doctor if symptoms worsen. Uses Of CLINVIVA GEL Manage acne vulgaris How CLINVIVA GEL Works CLINVIVA GEL acts against the bacteria by binding to the 50S subunit of the bacterial ribosome (site of protein synthesis), which in turn manages protein synthesis and works against the infection-causing bacteria. How to use CLINVIVA GEL Apply CLINVIVA GEL as advised by your physician. It is for external use only. Wash your hands before use. Wash and dry the whole area, apply a thin film once daily to the skin where acne lesions appear and use enough to cover the entire affected area. In case of contact with the eyes, mouth or nostrils, rinse it off immediately and thoroughly with water. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration for you depending on your age, body weight and disease condition. It will be given to you by the doctor only if clearly needed. Consult your doctor before applying CLINVIVA GEL. name: Tretiva 40mg Capsule 10'S
description: Introduction About TRETIVA TRETIVA contains Isotretinoin, a retinoid medication specifically designed to manage severe acne in adults and children over 12 years of age. It is particularly effective for nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring when other anti-acne treatments have failed. Acne is a skin condition characterized by inflammatory spots, oily skin, and painful nodular lesions that commonly affect the face, chest, and back. Take TRETIVA exactly as prescribed by your doctor, following the recommended dose and duration. It is best taken with food, preferably at the same time each day, to reduce the chances of missing a dose. It may take a few weeks before you notice an improvement in your symptoms but continue taking the medication as directed to achieve optimal results. If your condition does not improve after several weeks, consult your doctor for further advice. This medication can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, so limit sun exposure and use sunscreen when outdoors. It may also make your skin more fragile, so avoid waxing or laser treatments during therapy. Dryness of the lips, mouth, and eyes is another potential side effect—stay hydrated and use moisturizers or lubricating eye drops as needed Common side effects include dry skin, rashes, and elevated liver enzymes. While these are generally mild and tend to subside as your body adjusts to the medication, inform your doctor if they persist or cause discomfort. TRETIVA is known to cause birth defects, so it should not be used during pregnancy or if you are planning to conceive. Always discuss your treatment plan with your doctor to ensure safety and effectiveness. Uses Of TRETIVA Severe acne in adults and children (older than 12 years of age) Benefits of TRETIVA for Acne: TRETIVA is highly effective in managing severe acne conditions such as nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring. It works by reducing the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, unclogging pores, and decreasing inflammation, which helps to clear up existing acne and prevent new breakouts. This leads to smoother, healthier skin and reduces the risk of long-term scarring. Additionally, it targets the underlying causes of severe acne, making it a reliable choice for those who have not responded to other treatments. Always consult your doctor to ensure it is suitable for your condition. How TRETIVA Works TRETIVA work by targeting the root causes of severe acne. They reduce the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, which helps prevent pores from becoming clogged. This, in turn, reduces the growth of acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Isotretinoin also promotes the turnover of skin cells, preventing the formation of new acne lesions. Together, these actions help clear up existing acne and reduce the chances of scarring, making it an effective treatment for stubborn or severe acne conditions. How to use TRETIVA Take TRETIVA exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the capsule whole with a glass of water; do not crush or chew it. It is recommended to take the capsule with food to improve absorption and reduce stomach discomfort. Take it at the same time each day to maintain consistent levels of the medication in your body. Follow the prescribed dosage and duration carefully. Do not stop the medication abruptly without consulting your doctor, even if your symptoms improve. Regular follow-ups and blood tests may be required to monitor your progress and ensure safe usage. Avoid alcohol, excessive sun exposure, and waxing or laser treatments during the treatment period. Use sunscreen and moisturizers as recommended by your doctor. What if I Forget to take TRETIVA: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose—do not double the dose to make up for it. Overdosage of TRETIVA – In case you or anybody else accidently take too much of TRETIVA, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. This medication can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, so limit sun exposure and use sunscreen when outdoors. It may also make your skin more fragile, so avoid waxing or laser treatments during therapy. Dryness of the lips, mouth, and eyes is another potential side effect—stay hydrated and use moisturizers or lubricating eye drops as needed Common side effects include dry skin, rashes, and elevated liver enzymes. While these are generally mild and tend to subside as your body adjusts to the medication, inform your doctor if they persist or cause discomfort. ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL is known to cause birth defects, so it should not be used during pregnancy or if you are planning to conceive. Always discuss your treatment plan with your doctor to ensure safety and effectiveness. Uses Of ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL Severe acne in adults and children (older than 12 years of age) Benefits of ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL for Acne: ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL is highly effective in managing severe acne conditions such as nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring. It works by reducing the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, unclogging pores, and decreasing inflammation, which helps to clear up existing acne and prevent new breakouts. This leads to smoother, healthier skin and reduces the risk of long-term scarring. Additionally, it targets the underlying causes of severe acne, making it a reliable choice for those who have not responded to other treatments. Always consult your doctor to ensure it is suitable for your condition. How ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL Works ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL work by targeting the root causes of severe acne. They reduce the production of excess oil (sebum) in the skin, which helps prevent pores from becoming clogged. This, in turn, reduces the growth of acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Isotretinoin also promotes the turnover of skin cells, preventing the formation of new acne lesions. Together, these actions help clear up existing acne and reduce the chances of scarring, making it an effective treatment for stubborn or severe acne conditions. How to use ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL Take ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the capsule whole with a glass of water; do not crush or chew it. It is recommended to take the capsule with food to improve absorption and reduce stomach discomfort. Take it at the same time each day to maintain consistent levels of the medication in your body. Follow the prescribed dosage and duration carefully. Do not stop the medication abruptly without consulting your doctor, even if your symptoms improve. Regular follow-ups and blood tests may be required to monitor your progress and ensure safe usage. Avoid alcohol, excessive sun exposure, and waxing or laser treatments during the treatment period. Use sunscreen and moisturizers as recommended by your doctor. What if I Forget to take ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose—do not double the dose to make up for it. Overdosage of ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL – In case you or anybody else accidently take too much of ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Symptoms of ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL overdose are severe headache, abdominal pain, nausea, dizziness, redness of face, vomiting, somnolence, irritability, and itching. Aim for at least 8–10 glasses daily. Use a Gentle Cleanser: Opt for a mild, fragrance-free cleanser to avoid further irritation. Avoid harsh soaps or scrubs that can strip the skin of natural oils. Moisturize Frequently: Apply a rich, non-comedogenic moisturizer to your face and body at least twice a day, especially after washing. Look for products with hydrating ingredients like hyaluronic acid or ceramides. Protect Your Lips: Use a moisturizing lip balm, preferably one with SPF, to prevent and treat cracked lips caused by dryness. Reapply as needed throughout the day. Avoid Long, Hot Showers: Hot water can strip your skin of its natural moisture. Take shorter showers with lukewarm water to minimize dryness. Humidify Your Environment: Use a humidifier in your home to add moisture to the air, especially during winter or in dry climates. Apply Sunscreen: Use a broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher daily to protect your sensitive skin from sun damage and prevent further dryness. Limit Exfoliation: Avoid physical or chemical exfoliants, as isotretinoin makes your skin more delicate and prone to irritation. Choose Gentle Fabrics: Wear soft, breathable fabrics like cotton to reduce friction and irritation on your dry skin. Seek Medical Advice: If dryness becomes severe or persistent despite home remedies, consult your doctor for additional treatment options or product recommendations. Birth defects such as abnormalities of the face, eyes, ears, skull, central nervous system, cardiovascular system, and thymus and parathyroid glands or IQ less than score of 85 have been reported in female patients who were pregnant or became pregnant while on therapy with isotretinoin. Therefore, ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL is considered unsafe for use during pregnancy. Women of childbearing potential must use a reliable contraceptive method to avoid becoming pregnant. If you accidentally became pregnant while taking this medicine, stop taking it and consult your gynaecologist for further evaluation. It is also not recommended for you to get pregnant for one month after stopping isotretinoin tablets because some medicine may still be left in your body. Consult your doctor before taking it. Breastfeeding CONTRAINDICATED It is not known whether this medicine is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects, nursing mothers should not receive ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL Driving and Using Machines USE WITH CAUTION Do not drive or operate machinery if you experience dizziness, drowsiness or decreased night vision after taking ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL. Alcohol CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR Avoid consuming alcohol while taking ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL as it may increase side effects. Inform your doctor if you have an habit of chronic alcoholism. Kidney USE WITH CAUTION ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL should be used with caution in patients with kidney problems. Consult your doctor before taking it. Liver CONTRAINDICATED ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL is not recommended for use in patients with liver disease. Consult your doctor before taking it. Allergy CONTRAINDICATED Do not take ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL if you are allergic to Isotretinoin, soya, peanuts or any of the other ingredients of this medicine. Lungs USE WITH CAUTION ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL should be used with caution in patients having asthma. Consult your doctor before taking it. Use In Pediatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR The use of isotretinoin tablets in pediatric patients less than 12 years of age has not been studied. The use of isotretinoin for severe recalcitrant nodular acne in adolescents ages 12 to 17 years under careful medical supervision. Extreme caution should be taken if the child is suffering from metabolic or structural bone disease. Use In Geriatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR There is no proper information about the use of ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL in elderly patients. Consult your doctor before taking it. Avoid Excessive Sun Exposure: Wear sunscreen and protective clothing as isotretinoin can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Moisturize Regularly: Use lip balms and non-comedogenic moisturizers to manage dryness of lips and skin. Use Effective Birth Control: Isotretinoin can cause severe birth defects. Do Not Donate Blood: Avoid donating blood while on isotretinoin and for at least a month after stopping it, as it can harm pregnant recipients. Follow Regular Check-Ups: Attend scheduled visits with your doctor for blood tests and monitoring. Avoid Waxing or Laser Treatments: Your skin is fragile during treatment and prone to scarring. Alcohol can increase the risk of liver problems, so limit or avoid it. Notify your doctor about severe dryness, mood changes, or unusual symptoms. Interactions A. Norethindrone, ethinyl Oestradiol) St. John’s wort (herbal medicine used to manage mental disorders) Other medicines used to manage acne like keratolytic or exfoliative agents (Ex. salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide) Synopsis Drug : Isotretinoin Pharmacological Category : Retinoids Therapeutic Indication : Severe acne Dosage Forms : Tablet, Soft gel Capsule, Capsule More Information Relevant Health Articles – Hormonal Acne: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment Anti-Acne Food: Eat Healthy To Heal Acne -Infographic FAQs About ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL Q: What is ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL used for? A: Temporary hair thinning or hair loss can occur in some individuals during treatment. This side effect typically resolves after completing the course. If hair loss persists, consult your doctor. Q: Can I drink alcohol while taking ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL? A: It is advised to avoid alcohol while taking ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL, as it can increase the risk of liver damage and worsen side effects like dizziness or drowsiness. Consult your doctor if you experience irregularity in your periods during management with ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL. Is ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL safe to take in pregnancy? No. ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL is not recommended for use in pregnant women and women planning a pregnancy. Inform your doctor if you become pregnant during management with ACTAME 20 SOFTGEL. name: BENCLEAR A Gel 15gm
description: Introduction About BENCLEAR A GEL BENCLEAR A GEL is a combination of Adapalene and Benzoyl peroxide which belongs to the group of medicines called Antiacne agents. It is used in the management of acne. Acne vulgaris (commonly known as acne) is an inflammatory skin condition that occurs when the hair follicles present in the skin are clogged with excess oil and/or dead skin cells. It can also be aggravated by few bacteria (such as Propionibacterium acnes) and is highly common among on the teenagers and the young adults. It primarily affects the face, upper arms, trunk or back and is often characterized by pus-filled pimples, red bumps with inflammatory and non-inflammatory lesions. BENCLEAR A GEL is suitable for use both in adults and in children (aged 9 years or older). Apply a thin layer of BENCLEAR A GEL on the affected skin areas. Avoid contact of this medicine with your eyes, mouth, ears, nose or with open wounds. You must also protect your skin against sun light and against other light sources (such as UV lamps). Do not use BENCLEAR A GEL if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. BENCLEAR A GEL can be used in breastfeeding women if required. The most common side effects of using BENCLEAR A GEL are dry skin, mild burning sensation and skin irritation, redness or scaling. Consult your doctor if they trouble you. Uses Of BENCLEAR A GEL It is used in adults, children and in adolescents (aged 9 years or older) to: Manage acne How BENCLEAR A GEL Works BENCLEAR A GEL is a combination of two medicines namely, adapalene and benzoyl peroxide. Adapalene is a topical retinoid (a type of vitamin A). It modulates the skin cell cycle and manages the accumulation of excess sebum (natural oil produced by the skin) and dead skin cells on the hair follicles of the skin. It also reduces inflammation on the skin. Benzoyl peroxide is a keratolytic agent with antimicrobial properties. It improves skin’s tendency to exfoliate the dead skin cells naturally. It also reduces the number of acne-causing bacteria on the skin which can reduce the further spread of acne. Collectively, they unclog the hair follicles of the skin and exfoliates dead skin cells which reduces acne breakouts. How to use BENCLEAR A GEL Apply a thin layer of this medicine on the affected skin areas or as directed by the physician. It is for topical use only. Wash your hands before and after application. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and health condition. Avoid contact of BENCLEAR A GEL with your eyes, mouth, ears, nose, hair or with open wounds (cuts, scrapes or sunburn). Side Effects Of BENCLEAR A GEL Common Dry skin Skin redness and scaling Burning sensation of the skin Skin irritation Uncommon Itching of the skin (pruritus) Sunburn Rare Stop using BENCLEAR A GEL and consult your doctor immediately if you experience: Signs of allergic reaction (such as severe skin rash with itching of body parts, swelling of the eyes, face, lips or tongue causing throat tightness and breathing difficulties and feel faint) How To Manage Side Effects Skin redness and irritation: Place an icepack on the affected skin areas to ease the irritation. Avoid using harsh chemicals or soaps on the affected areas. Wear protective loose-fitting clothes while going outdoors. Regularly moisturize your skin. Avoid exposing your skin towards direct sunlight. If the condition did not improve, contact your doctor. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy BENCLEAR A GEL is not recommended for use in pregnant women. Therefore, inform your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. If you became pregnant while using this medicine, stop using it and contact your doctor immediately. Breastfeeding BENCLEAR A GEL can be used in breastfeeding women. However, do not apply this medicine on your chest to avoid exposing this medicine to the nursing infant. Allergy Talk to your doctor if you are allergic to Adapalene or Benzoyl peroxide. Others BENCLEAR A GEL is not recommended for use if you: Have any cuts, scrapes, sunburn or eczema at the site of application Use in Pediatrics: BENCLEAR A GEL can be used in children and adolescents (aged 9 years or older) if advised by the physician. Therefore, consult your doctor before using it. Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Before using BENCLEAR A GEL, inform your doctor if you are using any of the following: Other anti-acne medicines (such as clindamycin) Skin cosmetics (such as hair perming solutions, astringents, toners, shaving lotion, abrasive soaps or cleansers) Overdosage: If you or anyone else applied excessive amount of BENCLEAR A GEL, rinse your skin with plenty of cold water. If irritation persists, consult your doctor. Synopsis Drug : Adapalene, Benzoyl peroxide Pharmacological Category : Retinoid-like compounds, Topical Antibiotics Therapeutic Indication : Acne vulgaris Dosage Forms : Topical Gel More Information Keep BENCLEAR A GEL out of reach of children Store BENCLEAR A GEL at room temperature FAQs About BENCLEAR A GEL Will BENCLEAR A GEL be more effective if I overuse it? No. Do not overuse this medicine. If you use more, you will not get rid of acne quicker. Instead, it may make your skin more irritated and red. Therefore, only apply the quantity mentioned by your doctor. What are the side effects of using BENCLEAR A GEL? BENCLEAR A GEL is generally safe with limited or no side effects. However, you may experience skin dryness, redness or irritation after applying this medicine. Contact your doctor if it troubles you. What is the use of BENCLEAR A GEL? BENCLEAR A GEL is used in the management of acne. How BENCLEAR A GEL works? BENCLEAR A GEL manages the accumulation of excess sebum (natural oil produced by the skin) and dead skin cells on the hair follicles of the skin. It also reduces inflammation on the skin and improves skin’s tendency to exfoliate the dead skin cells naturally. It also reduces the number of acne-causing bacteria on the skin which can reduce the further spread of acne. How to use BENCLEAR A GEL? BENCLEAR A GEL is for external use only. Take the required quantity of the medicine and apply on the affected skin areas. Avoid contact of this medicine with your eyes, ears, nose or any other mucous membranes. How long does it take for BENCLEAR A GEL to work? It may take up to 2-3 weeks for BENCLEAR A GEL to show improvement in your skin condition. However, this period may vary from person-to-person depending upon the skin condition. How long should I use BENCLEAR A GEL? Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and health condition. You need to use BENCLEAR A GEL for the stipulated duration prescribed by your doctor. Failing to do so may not result in adequate response. What to do if I forgot to apply BENCLEAR A GEL? If you forgot to apply BENCLEAR A GEL, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is time for the next application, skip the missed one and apply the next dose. Do not excessively apply BENCLEAR A GEL to compensate the missed doses. Is BENCLEAR A GEL safe? BENCLEAR A GEL is safe at doses prescribed by the physician. Therefore, do not alter the dose of BENCLEAR A GEL without consulting your doctor. Can I stop using BENCLEAR A GEL without consulting your doctor? No. You should not stop using BENCLEAR A GEL without consulting your doctor as it may reduce its effectiveness. Therefore, apply BENCLEAR A GEL for the stipulated duration recommended by your doctor to achieve maximum results. Can BENCLEAR A GEL be used in pregnant women? BENCLEAR A GEL is not recommended for use in pregnant women. Therefore, inform your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. description: Introduction About ZIT 10 CAPSULE ZIT 10 CAPSULE contains Isotretinoin, a retinoid medication specifically designed to manage severe acne in adults and children over 12 years of age. It is particularly effective for nodular acne, conglobate acne, and acne prone to permanent scarring when other anti-acne treatments have failed. name: COSMELITE Cream 25gm
description: Introduction About COSMELITE CREAM COSMELITE CREAM is a combination of Hydroquinone, Tretinoin, Mometasone furoate which belongs to the group of medicines called Depigmenting agents, Retinoids and Corticosteroids respectively. It is used in adults for the management of moderate to severe melasma (dark spots on the skin) in association with sun-avoidance measures, like using sunscreens and wearing protective clothing. Melasma is one of the most frequently acquired hyperpigmentation (excess melanin production) disorders with symptoms such as symmetrical brown patches on sun exposed areas mainly on face. It is advised to avoid exposure to sun during management with COSMELITE CREAM for better results. While going out apply sunscreens and wear full covering protective clothes. Before using COSMELITE CREAM inform your doctor if you have any liver, kidney, lung or heart diseases. Safety and efficacy of COSMELITE CREAM is not established in pregnant women and in children below 12 years of age. Ask for your doctor’s advice before using. COSMELITE CREAM should be used with caution in breastfeeding women. The most common side effects of using COSMELITE CREAM are mild burning, stinging, redness and dryness. Consult your doctor if any of the symptoms worsen or doesn’t improve. Uses Of COSMELITE CREAM It is used in adults to Manages moderate to severe melasma (dark spots on the skin) How COSMELITE CREAM Works COSMELITE CREAM helps in managing melasma where Hydroquinone is a skin bleaching agent that blocks enzyme tyrosinase which is responsible for the production of melanin that cause pigmentation. Thus, it helps for fading of dark spots in skin. Tretinoin helps to recover the damage to the skin caused by sun exposure (photodamage) by thickening skin layer and loss of keratinized cells.it helps to rejuvenate the skin. Mometasone furoate blocks prostaglandin synthesis and reduces redness, swelling and itching caused by tretinoin and other skin infections. How to use COSMELITE CREAM Apply COSMELITE CREAM as advised by your physician. It is for external use only. Wash your hands before and after applying COSMELITE CREAM. Wash your face with a mild soap and dry properly. Apply COSMELITE CREAM at night and gently massage it in until it is absorbed. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, mouth, mucous membrane. Avoid exposure to sunlight while using this medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition. Side Effects Of COSMELITE CREAM Common Mild burning Stinging Redness Dryness Stop using COSMELITE CREAM and consult your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following: Infraorbital and paranasal fissures How To Manage Side Effects Application Site Reactions Apply cool compress or wet cloth over affected area. Avoid hot bath because hot water can irritate your skin further. Do not scratch the affected area. Use protective clothing when going outdoors. Regularly moisturize your skin and apply calamine lotion as a coolant. Contact doctor if it is not subsiding. Dry Skin Drink plenty of water, milk, honey and stay hydrated. Apply sunflower oil, coconut oil ,aloe vera or petroleum jelly to moisturize skin. Contact doctor if it doesn’t improve. Warning & Precautions Pregnancy CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR The safety and efficacy of COSMELITE CREAM is not being established in pregnant women. Consult with your doctor before using. Breastfeeding USE WITH CAUTION COSMELITE CREAM should be used with caution in breast feeding women. Consult with your doctor before using. Allergy CONTRAINDICATED Do not use COSMELITE CREAM if you are allergic to Hydroquinone, Tretinoin, Mometasone or any other constituents of this medicine. Consult your doctor before using. Use In Pediatrics CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR The safety and efficacy of COSMELITE CREAM is not being established in children below 12 years of age. Consult your doctor before using COSMELITE CREAM. Interactions A. Drug-Drug interactions: Before using COSMELITE CREAM, inform your doctor if you are taking, have taken or might take any other medicine, including prescription, non-prescription or any herbal medicine. Overdosage: If you or anyone else accidentally ingests or apply too much of COSMELITE CREAM, consult your doctor immediately. The use of isotretinoin for severe recalcitrant nodular acne in adolescents ages 12 to 17 years under careful medical supervision. Norethindrone, ethinyl Oestradiol) St. John’s wort (herbal medicine used to manage mental disorders) Other medicines used to manage acne like keratolytic or exfoliative agents (Ex. salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide) Synopsis Drug : Isotretinoin Pharmacological Category : Retinoids Therapeutic Indication : Severe acne Dosage Forms : Tablet, Soft gel Capsule, Capsule More Information Relevant Health Articles – Hormonal Acne: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment Anti-Acne Food: Eat Healthy To Heal Acne -Infographic FAQs About GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE Q: What is GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE used for? A: GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE is used to manage severe acne (nodular or cystic acne) that does not respond to other treatments like antibiotics. It works by reducing oil production in the skin and preventing clogged pores. Q: How should I take GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE? A: Take GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE as prescribed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily with food. Swallow the capsule whole with water, and avoid breaking or crushing it. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully for the best results. Q: What are the common side effects of GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE? A: Common side effects include dry skin, chapped lips, dry eyes, nosebleeds, and mild stomach discomfort. If you experience severe reactions like mood changes, persistent headaches, or vision problems, consult your doctor immediately. Q: Can GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE be taken during pregnancy? A: No, GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE should not be taken during pregnancy as it can cause severe birth defects. Women of childbearing age must use effective contraception during and at least one month after treatment. Q: Is GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE safe for long-term use? A: Isotretinoin is not usually prescribed for long-term use due to its potential side effects. Treatment duration is typically limited to 16–20 weeks. Always follow your doctor’s advice regarding treatment duration. Q: Can I use cosmetics while on GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE? A: Yes, you can use non-comedogenic and fragrance-free cosmetics. Avoid abrasive cleansers, harsh exfoliants, or acne products containing benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid, as these may irritate your skin. Q: Does GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE cause hair loss? A: Temporary hair thinning or hair loss can occur in some individuals during treatment. This side effect typically resolves after completing the course. If hair loss persists, consult your doctor. Q: Can I drink alcohol while taking GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE? A: It is advised to avoid alcohol while taking GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE, as it can increase the risk of liver damage and worsen side effects like dizziness or drowsiness. Q: How long does it take for GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE to work? A: You may start noticing improvements within 4–8 weeks, but the full effects are usually seen after completing the treatment course. Be patient and continue using the medicine as prescribed. Q: What precautions should I take while using GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE? A: Avoid excessive sun exposure and use sunscreen. Do not donate blood during and for one month after treatment. Inform your doctor about any other medications or supplements you are taking. Use a reliable birth control to avoid becoming pregnant while taking GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE. Do not undergo cosmetic procedures such as skin waxing, dermabrasion, laser, or artificial UV light detanning while taking GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE without consulting your doctor. Q: Can GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE be used by men? A: Yes, GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE is safe for men to use for severe acne. However, male patients planning to father a child need not take special precautions, as isotretinoin does not affect sperm. Can GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE cause irregular periods? According to some studies, menstrual irregularity was observed during management follow-ups. Consult your doctor if you experience irregularity in your periods during management with GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE. Is GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE safe to take in pregnancy? No. GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE is not recommended for use in pregnant women and women planning a pregnancy. Inform your doctor if you become pregnant during management with GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE. It is not recommended to get pregnant for one month after stopping GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE management because some medicine may still be left in your body. Consult your doctor before taking it. Contraception must be used for a month before taking GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE, during management and for a month afterwards. Discuss with your doctor regarding suitable contraceptive methods. Cut down on extreme exercise and physical activity as GEONOIN 10MG CAPSULE can cause muscle and joint pain especially in children and teenagers taking up vigorous physical activity. description: Introduction About CLINMISKIN SOLUTION CLINMISKIN SOLUTION contains Clindamycin, which belongs to the group of medicines called Antibiotics. It is used in the management of acne vulgaris. Acne vulgaris is a common skin condition that occurs when hair follicles get blocked with oil and dead skin cells. Symptoms include whiteheads, blackheads, small red, tender bumps, pimples, and pus-filled lumps on the skin. Before applying CLINMISKIN SOLUTION, inform your doctor if you have or ever had diarrhea, bloody diarrhea and pseudomembranous colitis. CLINMISKIN SOLUTION is not recommended for use if you have a history of regional enteritis (inflammation of the small intestine), ulcerative colitis (inflammation of the large intestine) or antibiotic-associated colitis. CLINMISKIN SOLUTION should be used with caution during pregnancy or by breastfeeding women only if clearly needed. The safety and effectiveness of CLINMISKIN SOLUTION in children under the age of 12 has not been established. The most common side effects of applying CLINMISKIN SOLUTION are burning, itching, and redness of the skin. Consult your doctor if symptoms worsen. Uses Of CLINMISKIN SOLUTION Manage acne vulgaris How CLINMISKIN SOLUTION Works CLINMISKIN SOLUTION acts against the bacteria by binding to the 50S subunit of the bacterial ribosome (site of protein synthesis), which in turn manages protein synthesis and kills the infection-causing bacteria. How to use CLINMISKIN SOLUTION Apply CLINMISKIN SOLUTION as advised by your physician. It is for external use only. Wash your hands before use. Wash and dry the whole area, apply a thin film once daily to the skin where acne lesions appear and use enough to cover the entire affected area. In case of contact with the eyes, mouth or nostrils, rinse it off immediately and thoroughly with water. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration for you depending on your age, body weight and disease condition. Side Effects Of CLINMISKIN SOLUTION Common Burning, itching or abnormal redness of the skin at the application site Scaling, pain, dryness and skin irritation at the application site Uncommon Abdominal pain Diarrhea Oily skin Rare Antibiotic-associated colitis Stop applying CLINMISKIN SOLUTION and contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following side effects: Allergic symptoms (e.g., rashes, itchiness, difficulty in breathing or eye swelling) Severe or bloody diarrhea. (a sign of bowel inflammation, pseudomembranous colitis) Warning & Precautions Pregnancy The safety and effectiveness of CLINMISKIN SOLUTION in pregnant women or women planning to have a baby have not been established yet. It will be given to you by the doctor only if clearly needed. Consult your doctor before applying CLINMISKIN SOLUTION. Breastfeeding CLINMISKIN SOLUTION should be used with caution in breastfeeding women as it is not known if the medicine is excreted in human milk. Your doctor will decide whether to discontinue nursing or the medicine, considering the benefits to the mother and baby. If it is applied to the chest, care should be taken to avoid accidental ingestion by the infant. Consult your doctor before applying CLINMISKIN SOLUTION.
